title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁 Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three
translations.idiomatic: the 53th year of Biographies

sentences.zh: 王神念羊侃羊鴉仁

translations.literal: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, and Yang Ren

sentences.zh: 王神念，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shennian was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shennian was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少好儒術，尤明內典。

translations.literal: In youth he loved Confucian arts and was especially clear in inner scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he loved Confucian learning and was especially versed in Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 仕魏位潁川太守，與子僧辯據郡歸梁，封南城縣侯。

translations.literal: He served Wei in the post of Administrator of Yingchuan; with his son Senbian he held the commandery and submitted to Liang, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nancheng District.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Wei as Administrator of Yingchuan; he and his son Senbian held the commandery and went over to the Liang, for which he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 曆安成、武陽、宣城內史，皆著政績。

translations.literal: He successively served as Interior Minister of Ancheng, Wuyang, and Xuancheng, and in each post achieved notable administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Interior Minister of Ancheng, Wuyang, and Xuancheng, distinguishing himself in each post.

sentences.zh: 後為青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 神念性剛正，所更州郡必禁止淫祠，時青州東北有石鹿山臨海，先有神廟祅巫，欺惑百姓，遠近祈禱，糜費極多。

translations.literal: Shennian's nature was stern and upright; in every province and commandery he passed through he invariably banned licentious shrines. At that time in the northeast of Qing Province there was Stone Deer Mountain facing the sea; formerly there had been a spirit temple and heterodox shamans who deceived and misled the common people, and from near and far they prayed, wasting resources to an extreme degree.
translations.idiomatic: Shennian was stern and upright by nature; in every province and commandery he held office he banned illicit shrines. In the northeast of Qing Province stood Stone Deer Mountain by the sea, where a spirit temple and shamans had long misled the people; worshippers came from far and wide and spent fortunes in offerings.

sentences.zh: 及神念至，便令毀撤，風俗遂改。

translations.literal: When Shennian arrived, he immediately ordered it destroyed and removed, and local custom was thereby changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shennian took office he had the shrine torn down, and local custom changed at once.

sentences.zh: 後徵為右衛將軍，卒于官，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as General of the Right Guard; he died in office, and his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to serve as General of the Right Guard and died in office; his posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 及元帝初，追贈侍中、中書令，改諡忠公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yuan's reign he was posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat, and his posthumous title was changed to Duke of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Yuan's reign he was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat, and his posthumous title was changed to Loyal Duke.

sentences.zh: 神念少善騎射，及老不衰。

translations.literal: Shennian from youth was skilled in mounted archery, and even when old he did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Shennian had been skilled in horsemanship and archery since youth, and even in old age he had not lost his edge.

sentences.zh: 嘗于武帝前手執二刀楯，左右交度，馭馬往來，冠絕群伍。

translations.literal: Once before Emperor Wu he held two sabers and shields in his hands, crossing them left and right, driving his horse back and forth, surpassing all the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once before Emperor Wu he took two sabers and shields in hand, crossing them left and right as he drove his horse to and fro—a feat unmatched in the whole company.

sentences.zh: 時復有楊華者，能作驚軍騎，亦一時妙捷，帝深賞之。

translations.literal: At the same time there was also Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry maneuvers; he too was a marvel of agility for the age, and the Emperor deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry feats—another marvel of the day whom the Emperor greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 華本名白花，武都仇池人。

translations.literal: Hua's original name was Bai Hua; he was a man of Chouchi in Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had originally been named Bai Hua and came from Chouchi in Wudu.

sentences.zh: 父大眼為魏名將。

translations.literal: His father Dahuan was a famous general of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dahuan was a celebrated Wei general.

sentences.zh: 華少有勇力，容貌瑰偉，魏胡太后逼幸之。

translations.literal: Hua in youth had courage and strength, and his appearance was magnificent; Empress Dowager Hu of Wei forced her favor upon him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hua was brave and powerfully built, with a striking appearance; Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei took him as her lover.

sentences.zh: 華懼禍，及大眼死，擁部曲，載父屍，改名華，來降。

translations.literal: Hua feared disaster; when Dahuan died he gathered his troops, loaded his father's corpse, changed his name to Hua, and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ruin, Hua waited until Dahuan died, then gathered his followers, bore his father's body away, changed his name to Hua, and defected to the Liang.

sentences.zh: 胡太后追思不已，為作楊白花歌辭，使宮人晝夜連臂蹋蹄歌之，聲甚淒斷。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Hu could not cease her longing and composed the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua, ordering palace women day and night to link arms and stamp their feet singing it; the sound was exceedingly mournful and broken.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu could not stop mourning him; she had the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua written and set palace women to link arms and stamp their feet in song day and night—the melody was heartbreakingly sad.

sentences.zh: 華後位太子左衛率，卒于侯景軍中。

translations.literal: Hua later held the post of Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's army.
translations.idiomatic: Hua later served as Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's forces.

sentences.zh: 神念長子遵業，位太僕卿。

translations.literal: Shennian's eldest son Zunye held the post of Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Shennian's eldest son Zunye rose to Minister Coachman.

sentences.zh: 次子僧辯。

translations.literal: The second son was Senbian.
translations.idiomatic: His second son was Senbian.

sentences.zh: 僧辯字君才，學涉該博，尤明左氏春秋。

translations.literal: Senbian's style name was Juncai; his learning ranged broadly and was comprehensive, and he was especially clear in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian, styled Juncai, was broadly learned and especially expert in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 言辭辯捷，器宇肅然，雖射不穿劄，而有陵雲之氣。

translations.literal: His words were eloquent and quick, his bearing stern; although in archery he could not pierce a writing slip, he had a spirit that soared above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with eloquence and quick wit and bore himself with grave dignity; though his archery could not pierce a writing slip, he had the air of one who might rise above the clouds.

sentences.zh: 元帝為江州刺史，僧辯隨府為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Inspector of Jiang Province, Senbian followed the headquarters as Central Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Yuan was Inspector of Jiang Province, Senbian served on his staff as Central Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 時有安成望族劉敬躬者，田間得白蛆化為金龜，將銷之，龜生光照室，敬躬以為神而禱之。

translations.literal: At that time there was a man of a prominent Ancheng clan named Liu Jinggong; in the fields he obtained white maggots that transformed into a golden tortoise. As he was about to melt it down, the tortoise gave birth to light that filled the room, and Jinggong took it for a spirit and prayed to it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man of a leading Ancheng clan, Liu Jinggong, found white maggots in his fields that turned into a golden tortoise. When he was about to melt it down, the tortoise emitted light that filled the room; Jinggong took it for a divine sign and began to worship it.

sentences.zh: 所請多驗，無賴者多依之。

translations.literal: Most of what was requested was fulfilled, and many ruffians attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his petitions were answered, and many ruffians rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 平生有德有怨者必報，遂謀作亂，遠近回應。

translations.literal: Those toward whom in his lifetime he had owed kindness or harbored resentment he invariably repaid; he then plotted rebellion, and near and far responded.
translations.idiomatic: He settled every old score, whether of kindness or resentment, then plotted rebellion; supporters rallied from near and far.

sentences.zh: 元帝命中直兵參軍曹子郢討之，使僧辯襲安成。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan ordered Central Direct Army Aide Cao Ziying to attack him and sent Senbian to strike Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan ordered Central Direct Army Aide Cao Ziying to suppress him and sent Senbian to raid Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 子郢既破其軍，敬躬走安成，僧辯禽之。

translations.literal: After Ziying had broken his army, Jinggong fled to Ancheng, and Senbian captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying routed his army; Jinggong fled to Ancheng, where Senbian captured him.

sentences.zh: 又討平安州反蠻，由是以勇略稱。

translations.literal: He also pacified the rebellious Man of An Province, and from this came to be known for courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He also put down rebellious Man tribes in An Province, and from then on was known for courage and strategy.

sentences.zh: 元帝除荊州，僧辯為貞毅府諮議參軍，代柳仲禮為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was relieved of Jing Province, Senbian became Advisory Aide of the Zhengyi Prefecture and replaced Liu Zhongli as Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan was assigned to Jing Province, Senbian became Advisory Aide of the Zhengyi Prefecture and replaced Liu Zhongli as Administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及侯景反，元帝命僧辯總督舟師一萬赴援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Emperor Yuan ordered Senbian to take overall command of ten thousand river troops to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Emperor Yuan put Senbian in command of ten thousand river troops to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 及至，台城陷沒，侯景悉收其軍實而厚加綏撫，遣歸竟陵。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Terrace City had fallen; Hou Jing gathered all his military stores and treated him generously with reassurance, then sent him back to Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the Terrace City had fallen; Hou Jing seized his supplies but treated him generously and sent him back to Jingling.

sentences.zh: 於是倍道兼行，西就元帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he traveled by double marches day and night and went west to join Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched day and night by forced marches to join Emperor Yuan in the west.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，以為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting under provisional authority, appointed him General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, acting under provisional authority, made him General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 及荊、湘疑貳，元帝令僧辯及鮑泉討之。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang showed disloyalty and wavering, Emperor Yuan ordered Senbian and Bao Quan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang provinces wavered in loyalty, Emperor Yuan sent Senbian and Bao Quan to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 時僧辯以竟陵間部下皆勁勇，猶未盡來，意欲待集然後上頓。

translations.literal: At that time Senbian, because the troops from the Jingling region were all stalwart and brave and had not yet all arrived, intended to wait until they were assembled before advancing to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian's crack troops from the Jingling region had not all yet arrived; he meant to wait until they were assembled before moving up to camp.

sentences.zh: 與泉俱入，使泉先言之，泉入不敢言。

translations.literal: He and Quan entered together; he had Quan speak first, but when Quan entered he did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: He and Quan went in together; Senbian had Quan speak first, but Quan entered and dared not say a word.

sentences.zh: 元帝問僧辯，僧辯以情對。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan questioned Senbian, and Senbian answered according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan questioned Senbian, who told him plainly how matters stood.

sentences.zh: 元帝性忌，以為遷延不去，大怒厲聲曰：「卿憚行拒命，欲同賊邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's nature was suspicious; he took it that Senbian was delaying and would not go, and in great anger said in a harsh voice: "You fear to march and refuse orders—you wish to join the rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was suspicious by nature; he took Senbian's delay for refusal to march and shouted in fury: "You shrink from the campaign and defy my orders—do you mean to join the rebels?

sentences.zh: 今唯死耳。」

translations.literal: Now there is only death."
translations.idiomatic: Death is all that awaits you now."

sentences.zh: 僧辯對曰：「今日就戮甘心，但恨不見老母。」

translations.literal: Senbian replied: "Today to accept execution I am willing at heart, but I regret only that I shall not see my old mother."
translations.idiomatic: Senbian answered: "I accept death today without regret; I grieve only that I shall not see my mother again."

sentences.zh: 帝自斫之，中其髀，流血至地，悶絕，久之方蘇。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself hacked at him, striking his thigh; blood flowed to the ground, and Senbian fainted, coming to only after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself struck at him and hit his thigh; blood pooled on the floor as Senbian fainted and lay long unconscious before reviving.

sentences.zh: 即送廷尉，並收其子侄並系之。

translations.literal: He was immediately sent to the Minister of Justice, and his sons and nephews were also seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent at once to the Minister of Justice, and his sons and nephews were seized and imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 其母脫簪珥待罪，帝意解，賜以良藥，故不死。

translations.literal: His mother removed her hairpins and earrings to await punishment; the Emperor's mind eased, and he bestowed good medicine, so Senbian did not die.
translations.idiomatic: His mother laid aside her hairpins and earrings to plead for mercy; the Emperor relented and gave him good medicine, so he survived.

sentences.zh: 會岳陽軍襲江陵，人情搔擾。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yueyang army raided Jiangling, and popular sentiment was agitated.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Yueyang army raided Jiangling and the city fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 元帝遣就獄出僧辯以為城內都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan sent to the prison to release Senbian and made him Metropolitan Commander within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had Senbian released from prison and made him commander of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 俄而岳陽奔退，而鮑泉力不能克長沙，帝命僧辯代之。

translations.literal: Before long the Yueyang forces fled in retreat, but Bao Quan's strength could not overcome Changsha; the Emperor ordered Senbian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Yueyang forces fled, but Bao Quan could not take Changsha; the Emperor replaced him with Senbian.

sentences.zh: 僧辯仍部分將帥，並力攻圍，遂平湘土。

translations.literal: Senbian thereupon deployed the generals and, joining forces in siege, pacified the Xiang region.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian redeployed his generals, concentrated the siege, and pacified the Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 還復領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On his return he again became General Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was again made General Who Leads the Army.

sentences.zh: 侯景浮江西寇，軍次夏首。

translations.literal: Hou Jing floated down the river westward in invasion; his army halted at Xiashou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sailed up the Yangzi to invade the west and camped at Xiashou.

sentences.zh: 僧辯為大都督，軍次巴陵。

translations.literal: Senbian served as Grand Commander; his army halted at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian served as Grand Commander with his army at Baling.

sentences.zh: 景既陷郢城，將進寇荊州，於是緣江屯戍望風請服。

translations.literal: After Jing had taken Ying City and was about to advance and invade Jing Province, the garrisons along the river accordingly submitted at the mere sight of his banners.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing took Ying City and prepared to march on Jing Province, garrisons along the river surrendered at the first sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 僧辯並沈公私船于水，分命眾軍乘城固守，偃旗臥鼓，安若無人。

translations.literal: Senbian sank both public and private boats in the water, ordered the various armies to mount the walls and hold firm, lowered banners and laid drums to rest, peaceful as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sank every public and private boat in the harbor, ordered his troops to man the walls and hold firm, and lowered banners and silenced drums so the city seemed deserted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊眾濟江，輕騎至城下，謂城中曰：「語王領軍，何不早降？」

translations.literal: The next day the rebel masses crossed the river; light cavalry came to the foot of the wall and said to those within: "Tell Wang the Army Leader—why not surrender early?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels crossed the river; light cavalry rode to the wall and called out: "Tell Wang the Army Leader—why not surrender now?"

sentences.zh: 僧辯使答曰：「大軍但向荊州，此城自當非礙。

translations.literal: Senbian sent a reply: "The great army need only head for Jing Province; this city of itself will be no obstacle.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sent back word: "March on to Jing Province; this city will not stand in your way.

sentences.zh: 僧辯百口在人掌握，豈得便降。」

translations.literal: Senbian's hundred mouths are in others' grasp—how could he simply surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: A hundred lives depend on me—how could I surrender so easily?"

sentences.zh: 景軍肉薄苦攻，城內同時鼓噪，矢石雨下，賊乃引退。

translations.literal: Jing's army pressed close in bitter assault; within the city drums and shouts rose at once, arrows and stones rained down, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's men pressed the assault at close quarters; the defenders beat drums and shouted as one, and arrows and stones rained down until the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元帝又命平北將軍胡僧佑率兵援僧辯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan again ordered Pacifier of the North General Hu Sengyou to lead troops to reinforce Senbian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan also ordered Pacifier of the North Hu Sengyou to reinforce Senbian with troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊復攻城不克，又為火艦燒柵，風不便，自焚而退。

translations.literal: That day the rebels again attacked the city without success; they also used fire ships to burn the palisades, but the wind was unfavorable and they burned themselves and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebels attacked again without success, then sent fire ships against the palisades; the wind turned against them, their own ships burned, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 有流星墮其營中，賊徒大駭，相顧失色。

translations.literal: A shooting star fell into their camp; the rebel soldiers were greatly terrified and looked at one another, their faces drained of color.
translations.idiomatic: A shooting star fell into their camp; the rebels were terrified and looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 賊帥任約又為陸法和所禽，景乃燒營夜遁，旋軍夏首。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Ren Yue was again captured by Lu Fahe; Jing then burned his camp and fled by night, wheeling his army back to Xiashou.
translations.idiomatic: Their commander Ren Yue was captured by Lu Fahe; Hou Jing burned his camp and fled by night, withdrawing his army to Xiashou.

sentences.zh: 元帝以僧辯為征東將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，封長寧縣公，命即率巴陵諸軍沿流討景。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan made Senbian General Who Campaigns East, with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Jiang Province, enfeoffing him as Duke of Changning District and ordering him at once to lead the Baling armies downriver to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made Senbian General Who Campaigns East with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Duke of Changning, and ordered him to lead the Baling armies downriver against Hou Jing at once.

sentences.zh: 攻拔魯山，仍攻郢，即入羅城。

translations.literal: He attacked and took Lushan, then continued to attack Ying and immediately entered the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Lushan, then pressed on to Ying and entered the outer city.

sentences.zh: 又有大星如車輪墜賊營，去地十丈變成火，一時碎散。

translations.literal: Again a great star like a carriage wheel fell into the rebel camp; ten zhang above the ground it turned into fire and at once shattered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Another great star like a carriage wheel fell into the rebel camp; ten zhang above the ground it burst into flame and shattered.

sentences.zh: 有龍自城出，五色光曜，入城前鸚鵡洲水中。

translations.literal: A dragon came forth from the city, its five-colored light dazzling, and entered the waters of Parrot Isle before the city.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon emerged from the city in dazzling five-colored light and plunged into the water off Parrot Isle.

sentences.zh: 景聞之，倍道歸建鄴。

translations.literal: When Jing heard of it, he traveled by double marches back to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing heard of these omens he marched day and night back to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 賊帥宋子仙等困蹙，求輸郢城，身還就景。

translations.literal: The rebel commanders Song Zixian and others, hard pressed, requested to hand over Ying City and return in person to join Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commanders Song Zixian and others, hard pressed, offered to surrender Ying City and return to Hou Jing in person.

sentences.zh: 僧辯偽許之。

translations.literal: Senbian falsely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 子仙謂為信然，浮舟將發，僧辯命杜龕鼓噪掩至，大破之，禽子仙、丁和等送江陵。

translations.literal: Zixian took it as truly believed; as he was about to set his boats afloat and depart, Senbian ordered Du Kan to drum and shout and rush upon them, routing them utterly; Zixian, Ding He, and others were captured and sent to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian took the offer at face value; as his boats were about to cast off, Senbian had Du Kan charge with drums and shouts, routed them completely, and sent Zixian, Ding He, and others as prisoners to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元帝命生釘和舌臠殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan ordered them nailed alive, their tongues cut out, and dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan had them nailed alive, their tongues cut out, and dismembered.

sentences.zh: 郢州既平，僧辯進師尋陽。

translations.literal: After Ying Province was pacified, Senbian advanced his army to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying Province was pacified, Senbian advanced on Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 軍人多夢周何二廟神云：「吾已助天子討賊。」

translations.literal: Many in the army dreamed that the gods of the Zhou and He temples said: "We have already aided the Son of Heaven in attacking the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Many soldiers dreamed that the gods of the Zhou and He temples said, "We have already aided the Son of Heaven in punishing the rebels."

sentences.zh: 自稱征討大將軍，並乘朱航。

translations.literal: They called themselves Grand Generals on Campaign and all rode vermilion boats.
translations.idiomatic: They called themselves Grand Generals on Campaign and rode vermilion boats.

sentences.zh: 俄而反曰：「已殺景。」

translations.literal: Before long they turned back and said: "Jing has already been killed."
translations.idiomatic: Soon they turned back and said, "Hou Jing is already dead."

sentences.zh: 同夢者數十百焉。

translations.literal: Those who shared the dream numbered in the tens and hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens and hundreds of men had the same dream.

sentences.zh: 元帝加僧辯侍中、尚書令、征東大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan added to Senbian's titles Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and Grand General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan further made Senbian Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, and Grand General Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 僧辯頻表勸進，並蒙優答。

translations.literal: Senbian repeatedly submitted memorials urging accession to the throne and each time received gracious replies.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian repeatedly urged Emperor Yuan to take the throne and each time received a gracious reply.

sentences.zh: 於是發江州直指建鄴，乃先命南兗州刺史侯瑱襲南陵、鵲頭等戍，並克之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he launched from Jiang Province straight for Jianye; he first ordered Inspector of Southern Yanzhou Hou Tian to raid the garrisons at Nanling, Quetou, and elsewhere, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched from Jiang Province straight for Jianye, first sending Inspector of Southern Yanzhou Hou Tian to storm the garrisons at Nanling, Quetou, and elsewhere—all fell.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳武帝率眾五萬出自南江，前軍五千行至盆口。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen the Martial Emperor had led fifty thousand men out from the Southern River; the vanguard of five thousand reached Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the future Chen Emperor had led fifty thousand men up the southern Yangzi; his vanguard of five thousand reached Penkou.

sentences.zh: 陳武名蓋僧辯，僧辯憚之。

translations.literal: Chen Wu's name overshone Senbian's, and Senbian feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's reputation overshadowed Senbian's, and Senbian was wary of him.

sentences.zh: 既至盆口，與僧辯會于白茅洲為盟。

translations.literal: When he reached Penkou, he met Senbian at White Reed Isle to form an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Penkou he met Senbian at White Reed Isle to swear alliance.

sentences.zh: 於是升壇歃血，共讀盟文，辭氣慷慨，皆淚下沾衿。

translations.literal: Thereupon they ascended the altar and drank the blood oath, together reading the alliance text; their words were impassioned, and all wept until their collars were wet with tears.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the altar, drank the blood oath, and read the alliance text together; their voices rang with passion, and all wept until their collars were soaked.

sentences.zh: 及發鵲頭，中江而風浪，師人咸懼。

translations.literal: When they set out from Quetou, mid-river wind and waves arose, and the troops were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When they sailed from Quetou, wind and waves struck mid-river and the troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 僧辯再拜告天曰：「僧辯忠臣，奉辭伐罪，社稷中興，當使風息；

translations.literal: Senbian bowed twice and addressed Heaven: "Senbian is a loyal minister, bearing the mandate to punish crime; if the altars of state are to be restored, the wind ought to cease.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian bowed twice toward Heaven and said: "Senbian is a loyal minister bearing the mandate to punish the wicked; if the dynasty is to be restored, let the wind fall still.

sentences.zh: 若鼎命中淪，請從此逝。」

translations.literal: If the tripod mandate is doomed to sink, I beg to perish here."
translations.idiomatic: If the Mandate is lost beyond recovery, let me perish here."

sentences.zh: 言訖風止，自此遂泛安流。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking the wind stopped, and from then on they sailed on calm waters.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, the wind died; from then on they sailed on calm waters.

sentences.zh: 有群魚躍水飛空引導，賊望官軍上有五色雲，雙龍挾艦，行甚迅疾。

translations.literal: A shoal of fish leaped from the water and flew through the air to guide them; the rebels saw above the imperial army five-colored clouds and two dragons flanking the ships, moving very swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Schools of fish leaped from the water and flew through the air as if to guide them; the rebels saw five-colored clouds above the imperial fleet and two dragons flanking the ships as they sped forward.

sentences.zh: 景自出戰於石頭城北，僧辯等大破之。

translations.literal: Jing himself came out to fight north of Stone City; Senbian and the others routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing came out to fight north of Stone City; Senbian and his allies routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 盧暉略聞景戰敗，以石頭城降。

translations.literal: Lu Huilue, hearing that Jing had been defeated in battle, surrendered Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huilue, hearing that Hou Jing had been defeated, surrendered Stone City.

sentences.zh: 僧辯引軍入據之。

translations.literal: Senbian led his army in and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian marched in and took possession.

sentences.zh: 景走朱方，僧辯命眾將入據台城。

translations.literal: Jing fled to Zhufang; Senbian ordered the various generals to enter and occupy the Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing fled to Zhufang; Senbian ordered his generals to enter and hold the Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 其夜軍人失火燒太極殿及東西堂。

translations.literal: That night soldiers by mischance set fire and burned the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and the Eastern and Western Halls.
translations.idiomatic: That night soldiers accidentally set fire to the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and the Eastern and Western Halls.

sentences.zh: 僧辯雖有滅賊之功，而馭下無法，軍人鹵掠，驅逼居人。

translations.literal: Although Senbian had the achievement of destroying the rebels, he had no law in governing subordinates; soldiers plundered and drove and pressed the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Though Senbian had destroyed the rebels, he could not control his men; soldiers looted and terrorized the populace.

sentences.zh: 都下百姓父子兄弟相哭，自石頭至於東城，被執縛者，男女裸露，衵衣不免。

translations.literal: The common people of the capital wept father to son and brother to brother; from Stone City to the Eastern City, those seized and bound—men and women stripped bare—could not keep even their undergarments.
translations.idiomatic: Capital families wept together from Stone City to the Eastern City; captives, men and women alike, were stripped naked and could not keep even their underclothes.

sentences.zh: 緣淮號叫，翻思景焉。

translations.literal: Along the Huai they cried out, turning their thoughts back to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Qinhuai they wailed that they had almost come to miss Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 僧辯命侯瑱、裴之橫東追景，偽行台趙伯超自吳松江降侯瑱，瑱送至僧辯，僧辯謂曰：「卿荷國重恩，遂復同逆，今日之事，將欲如何。」

translations.literal: Senbian ordered Hou Tian and Pei Zhiheng to pursue Jing eastward; the false Mobile Headquarters Zhao Bochao surrendered to Hou Tian from the Wusong River, and Tian sent him to Senbian. Senbian said to him: "You bore the state's heavy grace, yet again joined the rebellion—today's affair, what do you intend to do?
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sent Hou Tian and Pei Zhiheng east in pursuit of Hou Jing; Zhao Bochao of the rebel Mobile Headquarters surrendered to Hou Tian on the Wusong River, and Tian sent him to Senbian. Senbian said: "The state loaded you with favor, yet you rebelled again—what do you propose to do about today?

sentences.zh: 因命送江陵。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered him sent to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered him sent to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 伯超既出，僧辯顧坐客曰：「朝廷昔唯知有趙伯超，豈識王僧辯乎。

translations.literal: After Bochao had gone out, Senbian turned to the seated guests and said: "The court in former days knew only that there was Zhao Bochao—how would it have known Wang Senbian?
translations.idiomatic: After Bochao had left, Senbian turned to his guests and said: "The court once knew only Zhao Bochao—who had ever heard of Wang Senbian?

sentences.zh: 社稷既傾，為我所復，人之興廢，亦復何常。」

translations.literal: The altars of state have already toppled, yet we have restored them; the rise and fall of men—how is that ever constant?"
translations.idiomatic: The realm had collapsed, yet we have raised it up again; who among mortals can count on lasting fortune?"

sentences.zh: 賓客皆前稱歎功德，僧辯戄然，乃謬答曰：「此乃聖上威德，群帥用命，老夫雖濫居戎首，何力之有焉。」

translations.literal: The guests all stepped forward praising his merit and virtue; Senbian was startled, then falsely answered: "This is the sovereign's august power and virtue, the commanders all obeying orders—though this old man indiscriminately occupies the head of the army, what strength have I?"
translations.idiomatic: The guests all stepped forward to praise his achievement; Senbian, taken aback, gave a dissembling reply: "This is the Son of Heaven's majesty and the generals' obedience—though I happen to lead the army, what credit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 於是逆寇悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebellious bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the rebel forces were wholly subdued.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位，授鎮衛將軍、司徒，加班劍二十人，改封永寧郡公，侍中、尚書令如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, he appointed him General Who Guards the Realm and Minister of Works, added twenty ceremonial swords to his escort, changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Yongning Commandery, and kept him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he made Senbian General Who Guards the Realm and Minister of Works, augmented his escort by twenty ceremonial swords, changed his title to Duke of Yongning commandery, and left him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat as before.

sentences.zh: 先是，天監中沙門釋寶志為讖云：「太歲龍，將無理。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianjian era, the monk Shi Baozhi made a prophecy saying: "In the year of the Dragon of Tai Sui, the general will be without reason.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Tianjian reign, the monk Baozhi uttered a prophecy: "When the Tai Sui year is the Dragon, the leader will lose legitimacy.

sentences.zh: 蕭經霜，草應死。

translations.literal: The Xiao clan meets frost; the grass should die.
translations.idiomatic: The House of Xiao passes through frost; the grass must wither.

sentences.zh: 餘人散，十八子。」

translations.literal: The rest of the people scatter; eighteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: The commoners disperse; "ten," "eight," and "son."

sentences.zh: 時言蕭氏當滅，李氏代興。

translations.literal: At the time it was said the Xiao clan would perish and the Li clan would rise in its place.
translations.idiomatic: People read the verses as foretelling the fall of the Xiao and the rise of the Li.

sentences.zh: 及湘州賊陸納等攻破衡州刺史丁道貴，而李洪雅又自零陵稱助討納。

translations.literal: When the Xiangzhou rebels Lu Na and others attacked and broke Hengzhou Inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya moreover from Lingling declared himself aiding in punishing Na.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Lu Na of Xiangzhou overran Hengzhou and its inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya proclaimed from Lingling that he had come to help crush Na.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷未達其心，詔征僧辯就宜豐侯循南征，為都督東上諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon the court did not fathom his heart; an edict summoned Senbian to join Marquis Xun of Yifeng in a southern campaign, making him Commander-in-Chief of all eastern forces.
translations.idiomatic: The court still misread his intentions and ordered Senbian to march south with the Marquis of Yifeng, appointing him commander of all eastern armies.

sentences.zh: 以陳武帝為都督西下諸軍事。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi was made Commander-in-Chief of all western-downward military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi was placed in command of all western forces.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳武讓都督于僧辯，僧辯不受，故元帝分為東西都督而俱南討焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen Wu had yielded the commandership to Senbian, but Senbian did not accept; therefore Emperor Yuan divided east and west commanderships and both marched south to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Wu had offered Senbian supreme command, which Senbian refused; Emperor Yuan therefore split command into eastern and western wings and sent both south.

sentences.zh: 尋而洪雅降納，納以為應符，於是共議拜洪雅為大將軍，尊事為主。

translations.literal: Soon Hongya surrendered to Na; Na took it as fulfillment of the prophecy, and they jointly deliberated to invest Hongya as Grand General and honor him as lord.
translations.idiomatic: Hongya soon joined Na, who took this as confirmation of the prophecy; the rebels then agreed to make Hongya their generalissimo and acknowledged him as their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 洪雅乘平肩大輿，傘蓋、鼓吹，羽儀悉備，翼從入長沙城。

translations.literal: Hongya rode a level-shoulder great carriage; parasols, canopies, drums and pipes—all regalia fully prepared—he entered Changsha city with wings of attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Hongya entered Changsha in a state carriage with parasols, musical escort, and full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 時納等據車輪，夾岸為城，士卒皆百戰之餘，器甲精嚴，徒黨勇銳，蒙沖鬥艦，亙水陵山。

translations.literal: At the time Na and others held Chelun, building walls on both banks; the soldiers were all veterans of a hundred battles, weapons and armor exquisitely strict, followers brave and sharp, covered raiders and fighting ships spanning water and overrunning hills.
translations.idiomatic: Na held Chelun, fortifying both banks; his troops were hardened veterans with superb arms, his followers fierce, and his covered ships lined the waterway from shore to hill.

sentences.zh: 時天日清明，初無雲霧，軍發之際，忽然風雨，時人謂為泣軍，百姓竊言知其敗也。

translations.literal: At the time heaven's sun was clear and bright, at first without cloud or mist; at the moment the army set out, suddenly wind and rain—people of the time called it a weeping army, and common people whispered that they knew defeat was coming.
translations.idiomatic: The sky had been clear, yet the moment the army marched a storm broke; people called it the army weeping, and locals whispered that defeat was foretold.

sentences.zh: 三月庚寅，有兩龍自城西江中騰躍升天，五色分明，遙映江水。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the third month, two dragons leapt from the river west of the city soaring up to heaven, five colors distinct, reflecting distantly in the river water.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's gengyin day, two dragons rose from the river west of the city into the sky, their five colors vivid against the distant water.

sentences.zh: 百姓咸仰面目之，父老或聚而悲，竊相謂曰：「地龍已去，國其亡乎。」

translations.literal: The common people all looked up at their faces; elders sometimes gathered and wept, whispering to one another: "The earth dragons have departed—will the state perish?
translations.idiomatic: People gazed up at them; some elders wept together and murmured: "The earth dragons have gone—surely the realm is doomed.

sentences.zh: 初，納造大艦，一名曰三王艦者，邵陵王、河東王、桂陽嗣王三人並為元帝所害，故立其像於艦，祭乙太牢，加其節蓋羽儀鼓吹，每戰輒祭之以求福。

translations.literal: Earlier, Na built a great ship called the Three Kings Ship—for the Prince of Shaoling, Prince of Hedong, and Prince of Guiyang, three men all killed by Emperor Yuan—therefore he erected their images on the ship, offering yi and ta lao sacrifices, adding their banners, canopies, regalia, drums and pipes; before each battle he would sacrifice to them seeking fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Na had built a great warship, the Three Kings Ship, for the three princes Shaoling, Hedong, and Guiyang whom Emperor Yuan had killed; he set up their images aboard, sacrificed oxen to them with full honors, and before every battle offered prayers for luck.

sentences.zh: 又造二艦，一曰青龍艦，一曰白虎艦，皆衣以牛皮，並高十五丈，選其中尤勇健者乘之。

translations.literal: He also built two ships—one called the Azure Dragon Ship, one called the White Tiger Ship—both clad in ox hide, each fifteen zhang high, selecting from among them the most courageous and strong to man them.
translations.idiomatic: He also built two tower ships, the Azure Dragon and the White Tiger, sheathed in ox hide and fifteen zhang tall, crewed by his fiercest warriors.

sentences.zh: 僧辯憚之，稍作連城以逼焉。

translations.literal: Senbian feared them, and slightly built linked ramparts to press upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian, wary of these vessels, began building linked fortifications to press in on them.

sentences.zh: 賊不敢交鋒，並懷懈怠。

translations.literal: The rebels did not dare cross blades, and all harbored slackness.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels would not engage and grew complacent.

sentences.zh: 僧辯因其無備，親執旗鼓以誡進止，群賊大敗，歸保長沙。

translations.literal: Senbian, because they were unprepared, personally took drum and banner to admonish advance and halt; the rebel host was greatly defeated and returned to defend Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian seized their negligence, personally directing the drums and banners; the rebels were routed and fled back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 僧辯乃命築壘圍之，而自出臨視。

translations.literal: Senbian then ordered building ramparts to besiege them, and himself went out to oversee in person.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian ordered siege works built and went out personally to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 賊知不設備，其党吳藏、李賢明等蒙楯直進，僧辯尚據胡床不為之動，指麾勇敢，遂斬賢明，賊乃退歸。

translations.literal: The rebels, knowing he was unguarded, his partisans Wu Zang, Li Xianming and others covered with shields advanced straight on; Senbian still sat on a folding camp chair unmoved, directing with bravery, and thereupon cut down Xianming—the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought him undefended; Wu Zang, Li Xianming, and others charged under shield cover. Senbian did not rise from his camp chair, coolly directing the fight until Xianming was slain and the attackers fell back.

sentences.zh: 初，陵納作逆，以王琳為辭，云：「若放琳則自服」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Na rebelled, he used Wang Lin as his pretext, saying: "If Lin is released, I will submit myself."
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Na first rebelled, he claimed he would surrender if Wang Lin were freed.

sentences.zh: 時眾軍未之許，而武陵王紀擁眾上流，內外駭懼。

translations.literal: At the time the various armies did not agree to it, while Prince Ji of Wuling gathered troops upstream; inside and outside were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies refused, even as Prince Ji of Wuling massed forces upriver; court and camp alike were terrified.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃遣琳和解之，湘州乃平。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan then sent Lin to mediate and reconcile; Xiangzhou was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan dispatched Wang Lin to negotiate; Xiangzhou was finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 因被詔會眾軍西討。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received an edict to assemble the armies for a western punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to gather the armies for the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋而武陵敗績。

translations.literal: Soon Wuling suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Wuling was soon crushed.

sentences.zh: 是時，齊遣郭元建謀襲建鄴，又遣其大將東方老等繼之。

translations.literal: At this time, Qi sent Guo Yuanjian plotting to raid Jiankang, and also sent its great general Dongfang Lao and others to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi sent Guo Yuanjian to strike at Jiankang, with General Dongfang Lao and others close behind.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝聞之，馳報江陵。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi heard of it and galloped to report to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi heard the news and rushed word to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元帝即詔僧辯急下赴援。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan immediately issued an edict to Senbian to hurry down to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan at once ordered Senbian to march down in haste to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 僧辯次姑孰，即留鎮焉。

translations.literal: Senbian halted at Gushu and immediately remained to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian halted at Gushu and garrisoned the position.

sentences.zh: 先命豫州刺史侯瑱築壘于東關以拒北軍，征吳郡太守張彪、吳興太守裴之橫會瑱而大敗之。

translations.literal: First he ordered Yuzhou Inspector Hou Tian to build ramparts at Dongguan to resist the northern army; he summoned Wu Commandery Inspector Zhang Biao and Wuxing Inspector Pei Zhiheng to join Tian and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He first had Hou Tian of Yuzhou fortify Dongguan against the northern advance, then called Zhang Biao and Pei Zhiheng to join him—and together they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 僧辯振旅歸建鄴。

translations.literal: Senbian shook out his troops and returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian marched his army triumphantly back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年二月，詔以僧辯為太尉、車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Chengsheng, an edict made Senbian Grand Commandant and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Chengsheng, Senbian was appointed Grand Commandant and General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 頃之丁母憂。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 母姓魏氏，性甚安和，善於綏接，家門內外莫不懷之。

translations.literal: His mother surnamed Wei; her nature was very peaceful and harmonious, skilled at soothing and receiving—within and without the household gate none did not cherish her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was of the Wei clan, gentle and gracious, skilled at keeping harmony; everyone in the household and beyond held her in affection.

sentences.zh: 初，僧辯下獄，母流淚徒行，將入謝罪，元帝不與相見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Senbian was imprisoned, his mother wept and went on foot, about to enter to beg forgiveness; Emperor Yuan did not grant her an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Senbian was once imprisoned, his mother walked barefoot in tears to plead for him, but Emperor Yuan refused to see her.

sentences.zh: 時貞惠世子有寵，母詣合自陳無訓，涕泗嗚咽，眾並矜之。

translations.literal: At the time the heir of Zhenghui had favor; the mother went to the hall stating she had failed in instruction, tears and mucus sobbing—everyone together pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: The heir of Zhenghui was then in favor; she went to the palace gate, confessing that she had failed as a mother, weeping until all present were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯罪免，母深相責厲，辭色俱嚴。

translations.literal: When Senbian's guilt was remitted, his mother deeply rebuked and admonished him, words and expression both stern.
translations.idiomatic: When Senbian was released, his mother rebuked him sharply, her words and manner unsparing.

sentences.zh: 雖克復舊都，功蓋宇宙，母恒自謙損，不以富貴驕物，朝野稱之，謂為明哲婦人。

translations.literal: Although he recovered the old capital, his merit covering heaven and earth, his mother always herself modest and self-diminishing, not using wealth and rank to be arrogant toward things; court and countryside praised her, calling her a wise and perceptive woman.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had retaken the capital with merit surpassing all measure, his mother remained humble and never vaunted their rank; court and country alike praised her as a woman of wisdom.

sentences.zh: 及亡，甚見湣悼，且以僧辯勳重，故喪禮加焉。

translations.literal: When she died, she was greatly seen in pity and mourning; moreover because Senbian's merit was heavy, therefore the funeral rites were augmented.
translations.idiomatic: At her death the court mourned her deeply, and because of Senbian's outstanding service her funeral honors were enhanced.

sentences.zh: 命侍中、謁者監護喪事，諡曰貞敬太夫人。

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Attendant and Herald to supervise the funeral affairs; her posthumous title was Lady Zhenjing, the Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants and imperial heralds were appointed to oversee the funeral, and she was posthumously titled the Reverent Lady Zhenjing.

sentences.zh: 靈柩將歸建康，又遣謁者至舟渚弔祭。

translations.literal: As the coffin was about to return to Jiankang, he again dispatched a Herald to the riverbank to mourn and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin was sent back to Jiankang, imperial heralds were again dispatched to the river landing to perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，魏遣兵及梁王察合眾將襲江陵，元帝征僧辯於建鄴，為大都督、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Wei sent troops and Liang Prince Cha combining hosts to strike Jiangling; Emperor Yuan summoned Senbian from Jiankang, making him Grand Commander-in-Chief and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That October Wei troops and Prince Cha of Liang joined forces to attack Jiangling; Emperor Yuan recalled Senbian from Jiankang as supreme commander and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未至，而荊州已滅。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Jingzhou had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could arrive, Jingzhou had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 及敬帝初即梁王位，僧辯預援立功，承制進驃騎大將軍、中書監、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing first ascended the Liang throne, Senbian beforehand aided and established merit; by provisional order he was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Commander-in-Chief of all internal and external military affairs, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing first took the Liang throne, Senbian's role in restoring order earned him promotion to General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, supreme commander, and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 與陳武帝參謀討伐。

translations.literal: Together with Chen Wudi he counseled on punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He and Chen Wudi planned the military campaigns together.

sentences.zh: 時齊文宣又納貞陽侯明以為梁嗣，與僧辯書，並貞陽亦頻與僧辯書，論還國繼統之事。

translations.literal: At the time Qi Wenzuan again installed Marquis Zhenyang Ming as Liang successor, writing to Senbian; Zhenyang also frequently wrote to Senbian, discussing returning to the state and inheriting the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Emperor Wenxuan now backed the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, as Liang's rightful heir; both the emperor and Ming wrote repeatedly to Senbian about restoring Ming to the throne.

sentences.zh: 僧辯不納。

translations.literal: Senbian did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian refused.

sentences.zh: 及貞陽與齊上党王高渙至東關，散騎常侍裴之橫軍敗，僧辯遂謀納貞陽，仍書定君臣之禮。

translations.literal: When Zhenyang and Qi's Prince of Shangdang Gao Huan reached Dongguan, Regular Attendant Pei Zhiheng's army was defeated; Senbian then plotted to install Zhenyang, still by letter fixing lord-and-minister rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Ming and the Prince of Shangdang, Gao Huan, reached Dongguan and Pei Zhiheng's force was defeated, Senbian resolved to welcome Ming back and confirmed their sovereign-minister relationship in writing.

sentences.zh: 因遣第七子顯、顯所生劉並弟子珍往充質，遣左戶尚書周弘正至曆陽迎明。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his seventh son Xian, Xian's birth-mother Liu, and his younger brother's son Zhen to serve as hostages; he sent Left Household Minister Zhou Hongzheng to Liyang to welcome Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his seventh son Xian, Xian's mother Lady Liu, and his nephew Zhen as hostages, and dispatched Zhou Hongzheng of the Left Household to Liyang to receive Ming.

sentences.zh: 又遣吏部尚書王通送啟，因求以敬帝為皇太子。

translations.literal: He again sent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Tong to deliver a memorial, thereby requesting that Emperor Jing be made Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wang Tong of the Ministry of Personnel with a memorial asking that Emperor Jing be confirmed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 明報書許之。

translations.literal: Ming replied by letter agreeing.
translations.idiomatic: Ming wrote back in agreement.

sentences.zh: 僧辯遣使送質於鄴，貞陽求度衛士三千。

translations.literal: Senbian sent envoys to deliver hostages to Ye; Zhenyang requested escort of three thousand guards.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian sent the hostages to Ye, while Ming asked for an escort of three thousand guards.

sentences.zh: 僧辯慮其為變，止受散卒千人而已，並遣龍舟法駕往迎。

translations.literal: Senbian feared they would foment trouble and accepted only a thousand scattered soldiers, nothing more, and also dispatched the dragon boat and imperial carriage to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing treachery, Senbian accepted only a thousand irregular troops and sent the imperial dragon boat to receive him.

sentences.zh: 貞陽濟江之日，僧辯擁烜中流，不敢就岸，末乃同會于江寧浦。

translations.literal: On the day Zhenyang crossed the river, Senbian held official banners midstream, not daring to approach shore; only at the end did they meet together at Jiangning Ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming crossed the Yangtze, Senbian waited midstream under imperial banners and would not come ashore until they finally met at Jiangning Ford.

sentences.zh: 明踐位，授僧辯大司馬，領太子太傅、揚州牧，餘如故。

translations.literal: When Ming took the throne, he invested Senbian as Grand Marshal, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Governor of Yangzhou; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned, Ming made Senbian Grand Marshal, also Grand Tutor to the crown prince and governor of Yangzhou, while his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝時為司空、南徐州刺史，因自京口舉兵襲之。

translations.literal: Chen Wudi was at the time Minister of Works and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou; therefore from Jingkou he raised troops to surprise-attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wudi, then Minister of Works and governor of Southern Xuzhou, marched from Jingkou to strike him by surprise.

sentences.zh: 僧辯常處石頭城，是日視事，軍人已踰城北而入，南門又白有兵來。

translations.literal: Senbian usually resided at Stone City; that day he was conducting business when soldiers had already crossed the city's north wall and entered; the south gate also reported troops coming.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian was usually at Stone City; that day, as he held court, soldiers were already coming over the north wall, and the south gate reported an approach.

sentences.zh: 僧辯與子頠遽走出合，計無所出，乃據南門樓拜請求哀。

translations.literal: Senbian and his son Yi hastily ran out of the hall; finding no way out, they then took the south gate tower, bowing and begging for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian and his son Yi fled the hall in panic; with no escape, they climbed the south gate tower and bowed in supplication.

sentences.zh: 陳武縱火焚之，方共頠下就執。

translations.literal: Chen Wu set fire and burned it; only then together did Yi come down and submit to arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu set the tower afire; only then did Yi come down with his father and they were seized.

sentences.zh: 陳武謂曰：「我有何辜，公欲與齊師賜討。」

translations.literal: Chen Wu said to him: "What guilt have I, that my lord would join with Qi troops to grant punishment and attack?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu said: "What have I done that you would bring Qi armies against me?

sentences.zh: 又曰：「何意全無防備。」

translations.literal: He also said: "How is it that there is wholly no defense?"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Why were you completely unprepared?"

sentences.zh: 僧辯曰：「委公北門，何謂無備？」

translations.literal: Senbian said: "I entrusted the north gate to you—how can you say there was no defense?"
translations.idiomatic: Senbian replied: "I left the north gate to you—how is that no defense?"

sentences.zh: 是夜，及子頠俱被絞殺。

translations.literal: That night, he and his son Yi were both strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: That night he and his son Yi were strangled.

sentences.zh: 初，僧辯平建鄴，遣陳武守京口，推以赤心，結廉、藺之分。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Senbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Chen Wu to guard Jingkou, extending with a red heart, forming the bond of Lian and Lin.
translations.idiomatic: After Senbian pacified Jiankang, he placed Chen Wu at Jingkou in the trust of sworn friendship, like Lian Po and Lin Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 且為第三子頠許娶陳武章後所生女，未昏而僧辯母亡，然情好甚密，其長子顗屢諫不聽。

translations.literal: Moreover he betrothed his third son Yi to the daughter born to Chen Wu's wife Zhang; before marriage Senbian's mother died, yet their affection was very close; his eldest son Yan repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He even betrothed his third son Yi to Chen Wu's daughter by Lady Zhang; though Senbian's mother died before the wedding, the two remained intimate, despite repeated warnings from his eldest son Yan.

sentences.zh: 至是，會江淮人報云：「齊兵大舉至壽春」，僧辯謂齊軍必出江表，因遣記室參軍江旰以事報陳武，仍使整舟艦器械。

translations.literal: At this point, a person from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops in great force have reached Shouchun"; Senbian thought Qi army would surely come out onto the Jiang region, and therefore sent Recorder of the Headquarters Jiang Gan to report the matter to Chen Wu, still ordering him to put ships and weapons in order.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a man from the Jiang-Huai region reported that Qi was massing at Shouchun; Senbian assumed they would cross the Yangtze and sent his secretary Jiang Gan to inform Chen Wu and prepare the fleet.

sentences.zh: 陳武宿有圖僧辯志，乃聞命，留旰城中，銜枚而進。

translations.literal: Chen Wu had long harbored intent to plot against Senbian; upon hearing the order, he kept Gan in the city and advanced with gags in mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu had long planned Senbian's downfall; he kept Gan in the city and marched silently on Stone City.

sentences.zh: 知謀者唯侯安都、周文育而已，外人但謂江旰徵兵扞北。

translations.literal: Those who knew the plot were only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu; outsiders merely thought Jiang Gan was raising troops to repel the north.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu knew the real plan; everyone else thought Jiang Gan was simply mobilizing against the northern threat.

sentences.zh: 安都舟艦將趣石頭，陳武控馬未進。

translations.literal: Andu's ships and warships were about to make for Stone City; Chen Wu reined his horse and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: As Hou Andu's fleet bore down on Stone City, Chen Wu held his horse back and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 安都大懼，乃追陳武罵曰：「今日作賊，事勢已成，生死須決，在後欲何所望？

translations.literal: Andu was greatly afraid; he then pursued Chen Wu and cursed: "Today we play rebel—the situation is already settled; life and death must be decided; hanging back, what do you hope for?
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hou Andu galloped after Chen Wu and shouted: "We are rebels today and there is no turning back—if we fail we die together; what do you expect by hanging back?

sentences.zh: 若敗俱死，後期得免斫頭邪？」

translations.literal: If defeated we die together—do you think hanging back will spare you beheading?
translations.idiomatic: If we lose we all die—do you think hanging back will save your neck?

sentences.zh: 陳武曰：「安都嗔我。」

translations.literal: Chen Wu said: "Andu is angry at me."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu said: "Andu is furious with me."

sentences.zh: 乃敢進，遂克之，時壽春竟無齊軍，又非陳武之譎，殆天授也。

translations.literal: Only then did he dare advance, and thus captured it; at the time Shouchun ultimately had no Qi army, and it was not Chen Wu's stratagem—perhaps heaven conferred it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he advance and take the city; as it happened there were no Qi troops at Shouchun at all—it was no ruse of Chen Wu's, but almost as if heaven had granted him the moment.

sentences.zh: 顗承聖初位侍中，魏克江陵，隨王琳入齊，為竟陵郡守。

translations.literal: Yan in the beginning of Chengsheng held Palace Attendant; when Wei took Jiangling, he followed Wang Lin into Qi and served as Administrator of Jingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan became Palace Attendant early in the Chengsheng era; when Wei conquered Jiangling he went north with Wang Lin and served as governor of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 齊遣王琳鎮壽春，將圖江左。

translations.literal: Qi dispatched Wang Lin to garrison Shouchun, intending to scheme against the Jiang left bank.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Wang Lin to hold Shouchun, aiming to reconquer the south.

sentences.zh: 及陳平淮南殺琳，顗聞之，乃出郡城南登高塚上，號哭一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When Chen pacified Huainan and killed Lin, Yan heard of it; he then went south of the commandery city and climbed a high mound, wailing one great grief and expiring.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen conquered Huainan and killed Wang Lin, Yan climbed a mound south of the city, gave one great cry of grief, and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 顗弟頒，少有志節，恒隨梁元帝。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Ban, from youth had aspiration and integrity, always following Liang Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Ban was spirited from youth and always followed Emperor Yuan of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及荊州覆滅，入于魏。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was overthrown and destroyed, he entered into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell he passed into Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 僧辯既亡，弟僧智得就任約。

translations.literal: After Senbian had perished, his younger brother Sengzhi obtained Ren Yue's appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Senbian's death, his brother Sengzhi joined Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 敗走，僧智肥不能行，又遇害。

translations.literal: Defeated, he fled; Sengzhi was fat and could not walk, and again met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: In defeat Sengzhi fled, but he was too heavy to run and was killed.

sentences.zh: 僧智弟僧愔位譙州刺史，征蕭勃，及聞兄死，引軍還。

translations.literal: Sengzhi's younger brother Sengyin held the post of Qiaozhou Inspector, campaigning against Xiao Bo; when he heard of his elder brother's death, he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhi's brother Sengyin, governor of Qiaozhou, was campaigning against Xiao Bo when he heard of his brother's death and turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 時吳州刺史羊亮隸在僧愔下，與僧愔不平，密召侯瑱見禽。

translations.literal: At the time Wuzhou Inspector Yang Liang was subordinate under Sengyin, at odds with Sengyin; he secretly summoned Hou Tian and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang, governor of Wuzhou and nominally under Sengyin, resented him and secretly summoned Hou Tian—and was captured.

sentences.zh: 僧愔以名義責瑱，瑱乃委罪於將羊鯤斬之。

translations.literal: Sengyin held Tian accountable in name and principle; Tian then shifted blame onto his general Yang Kun and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyin rebuked Hou Tian on grounds of duty; Tian blamed his general Yang Kun and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 僧愔復得奔齊，與徐嗣徽等挾齊軍攻陳。

translations.literal: Sengyin again succeeded in fleeing to Qi; with Xu Sihui and others he leveraged Qi troops to attack Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyin escaped to Qi and, with Xu Sihui and others, brought northern troops against Chen.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，竄逸荒野，莫知所之，仰天歎曰：「讎恥不雪，未欲身膏野草，若精誠有感，當得道路，誓不受辱人手。」

translations.literal: The army was defeated; he fled into the wilds, none knowing where; looking up to heaven he sighed: "Vengeance-shame not yet cleared, I do not yet wish my body to grease the wild grass; if sincere devotion moves response, I should obtain a road—I swear not to accept disgrace at another's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he fled into the wilderness with no clear destination and cried to heaven: "My shame is unavenged—I am not ready to die in the weeds; if heaven hears sincerity, let a path open—I will never fall into enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 拔刀將自刎，聞空中催令急去，僧愔異之，勉力馳進，行一里許，顧向處已有陳人。

translations.literal: He drew his sword about to cut his own throat; he heard from mid-air an urgent command to go quickly; Sengyin marveled at it, strained his strength galloping forward; after traveling about one li, looking back at where he had been there were already Chen men.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword to kill himself, but heard a voice from the air bidding him flee; astonished, he forced himself onward, and a mile later looked back to see Chen soldiers where he had stood.

sentences.zh: 踰越江山，僅得歸齊。

translations.literal: Crossing over rivers and mountains, he barely succeeded in returning to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed rivers and mountains and barely made it back to Qi.

sentences.zh: 徐嗣徽，高平人，父雲伯自青部南歸，位終新蔡太守。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui, a man of Gaoping; his father Yunbo returned south from the Qing region, his post ending as Administrator of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sihui was from Gaoping; his father Yunbo had migrated south from the north and ended his career as governor of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，嗣徽歸荊州，元帝以為羅州刺史，及弟嗣宗、嗣產並有武用。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Sihui returned to Jingzhou; Emperor Yuan made him Inspector of Luozhou, and his younger brothers Sizong and Sichan both had martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Sihui went to Jingzhou, where Emperor Yuan made him governor of Luozhou; his brothers Sizong and Sichan were also capable soldiers.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽從征巴丘，以功為太子右衛率、監南荊州。

translations.literal: Sihui followed the campaign at Baqiu, and by merit became Right Guard Leader of the Crown Prince and Supervisor of Southern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui campaigned at Baqiu and was rewarded with the post of Right Guard of the Crown Prince and supervisor of southern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐州之亡，任秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At Xuzhou's fall, he was appointed Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuzhou fell he was made governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣產先在建鄴，嗣宗自荊州滅亡中逃得至都。

translations.literal: Sichan was first in Jiankang; Sizong from Jingzhou's destruction escaped and reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sichan was already in Jiankang; Sizong escaped the fall of Jingzhou and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 從弟嗣先即僧辯之甥，復為比丘慧暹藏，得脫俱還。

translations.literal: His younger cousin from the father's side Sixian was Senbian's sister's son; again as the monk Huixian he concealed them, and they obtained release and all returned together.
translations.idiomatic: Their cousin Sixian, Senbian's nephew, was hidden by the monk Huixian until all could flee and return together.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯見害，兄弟抽刀裂眥，志在立功，俱逃就兄嗣徽，密結南豫州刺史任約與僧辯故舊，圖陳武帝。

translations.literal: When Senbian met with harm, the brothers drew swords and split their canthi, their will set on establishing merit; all fled to join their elder brother Sihui, secretly joining Southern Yuzhou Inspector Ren Yue and Senbian's old associates, plotting against Chen Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: When Senbian was killed, the brothers swore blood vengeance and fled to Xu Sihui, secretly allying with Ren Yue of southern Yuzhou and Senbian's old friends to move against Chen Wudi.

sentences.zh: 帝遣江旰說之，嗣徽執旰送鄴乞師焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Jiang Gan to persuade them; Sihui seized Gan and sent him to Ye to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Jiang Gan to negotiate; Sihui seized him and sent him to Ye to request an army.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣帝授為儀同，命將應赴。

translations.literal: Qi Wenzuan Di invested him as Yitong, ordering generals to respond and go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi made him a Yitong and ordered troops to march to his support.

sentences.zh: 及石頭敗退，復請兵于齊，與任約、王曄、席皋同心度江。

translations.literal: When Shitou was defeated and withdrew, he again requested troops from Qi, and with Ren Yue, Wang Ye, and Xi Gao alike resolved to cross the Yangtze together.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Shitou and their retreat, he once more asked Qi for reinforcements, and together with Ren Yue, Wang Ye, and Xi Gao prepared to cross the Yangtze as one.

sentences.zh: 及戰敗，嗣徽墮馬，嗣宗援兄見害。

translations.literal: When they were defeated in battle, Sihui fell from his horse; Sizong came to aid his elder brother and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the battle was lost, Sihui was thrown from his horse; Sizong rushed to his brother's aid and was slain.

sentences.zh: 嗣產為陳武軍所禽，辭色不撓而死。

translations.literal: Sichan was captured by Chen Wu's army and died without yielding in speech or countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Sichan was taken by Chen Wu's troops; even under capture his bearing never broke, and he died unbowed.

sentences.zh: 任約、王曄得北歸。

translations.literal: Ren Yue and Wang Ye were able to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue and Wang Ye made it back to the north.

sentences.zh: 羊侃字祖忻，泰山梁父人也。

translations.literal: Yang Kan, styled Zuxin, was a man of Liangfu in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan, courtesy name Zuxin, was a native of Liangfu in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父祉，北史有傳。

translations.literal: His father Zhi has a biography in the History of the Northern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Zhi is given a separate biography in the Beishi.

sentences.zh: 侃少而瑰偉，身長七尺八寸，雅愛文史。

translations.literal: Kan from youth was magnificent and imposing; his body was seven feet eight inches in height, and he greatly loved literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Kan was striking in stature and bearing. He stood seven feet eight inches tall and had a cultivated love of letters and history.

sentences.zh: 弱冠隨父在梁州立功，初為尚書郎，以力聞。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he followed his father to Liang Province and performed meritorious service; he was first a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and became known for his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In early manhood he served with his father in Liang Province and won distinction; his first appointment was as a Masters of Writing gentleman, and he earned fame for his physical prowess.

sentences.zh: 魏帝常謂曰：「郎官謂卿為虎，豈羊質虎皮乎？

translations.literal: The Wei emperor often said to him: "The office gentlemen call you a tiger — can this be a sheep wearing a tiger's skin?
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor once asked him, "My officials say you are a tiger. Are you a sheep in a tiger's pelt?

sentences.zh: 試作虎狀。」

translations.literal: Try to assume the appearance of a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Show me a tiger's manner.

sentences.zh: 侃因伏，以手抉殿沒指。

translations.literal: Kan thereupon prostrated himself and, with his hand gouging into the palace floor, sank his fingers in.
translations.idiomatic: Kan dropped to all fours and dug his fingers into the stone floor of the hall until his knuckles disappeared from sight.

sentences.zh: 魏帝壯之，賜以珠劍。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor admired this and bestowed on him a pearl-hilted sword.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was so impressed that he awarded Kan a sword with a pearl-studded hilt.

sentences.zh: 正光中，秦州羌莫折念生據州反，仍遣其弟天生攻陷岐州，寇雍州。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, the Qiang Mo Zheniansheng of Qin Province seized the province and rebelled; he also sent his younger brother Tiansheng to attack and capture Qi Province, and raided Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang reign, the Qiang chieftain Mo Zheniansheng seized Qin Province in revolt and sent his brother Tiansheng to take Qi Province and harass Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 侃為偏將，隸蕭寶寅往討之，射殺天生，其眾即潰。

translations.literal: Kan served as a subordinate general under Xiao Baoyin on the punitive expedition; he shot and killed Tiansheng, and the enemy host at once collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a deputy under Xiao Baoyin, Kan joined the campaign, brought down Tiansheng with an arrow, and the rebel ranks broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 以功為征東大將軍、東道行台，領泰山太守，進爵钜平侯。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made General Who Conquers the East and Eastern Route Commissioner, concurrently Grand Administrator of Taishan, and advanced in rank to Marquis of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was appointed General Who Conquers the East and commissioner of the eastern route, made concurrent grand administrator of Taishan, and raised to Marquis of Juping.

sentences.zh: 初，其父祉恒使侃南歸，侃至是將舉濟、河以成先志。

translations.literal: At the outset, his father Zhi had constantly urged Kan to return south; Kan at this time was about to raise the banner in Ji and He to fulfill his father's earlier wish.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had long urged him to return to the south; now Kan prepared to raise forces in the Ji and He regions to fulfill that old pledge.

sentences.zh: 其從兄兗州刺史敦密知之，據州拒侃，侃乃率精兵三萬襲之，不克，仍築十餘城以守之。

translations.literal: His cousin Dun, Governor of Yan Province, learned of this in secret, held the province and resisted Kan; Kan then led thirty thousand picked troops to strike him, failed to take him, and still built more than ten fortified cities to hold the line.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Dun, governor of Yan Province, learned of the plan and barred the province against him. Kan led thirty thousand elite troops in a surprise attack but could not break him, and instead fortified more than ten garrison towns to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 梁朝賞授一與元法僧同。

translations.literal: The Liang court's rewards and appointments were identical to those granted Yuan Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang court honored him with the same titles and rank it had bestowed on Yuan Faseng.

sentences.zh: 魏帝聞之，使授侃驃騎大將軍、司徒、泰山郡公，長為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor heard of this and sent envoys to invest Kan as General of Fast Cavalry, Grand Mentor, Duke of Taishan Commandery, and to install him permanently as Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the Wei court, the emperor dispatched envoys offering Kan the posts of General of Fast Cavalry, Grand Mentor, Duke of Taishan commandery, and permanent governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 侃斬其使。

translations.literal: Kan beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Kan had the envoys executed.

sentences.zh: 魏人大駭，令僕射於暉率眾十萬及高歡、爾朱陽都等相繼而至。

translations.literal: The Wei people were greatly alarmed and ordered the Master of Writing Yu Hui to lead an army of one hundred thousand, with Gao Huan, Erzhu Yangdu, and others arriving in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court was shaken. They dispatched Master of Writing Yu Hui at the head of a hundred thousand men, followed in turn by Gao Huan, Erzhu Yangdu, and others.

sentences.zh: 柵中矢盡，南軍不進，乃夜潰圍而出。

translations.literal: Within the palisade arrows were exhausted; the southern army did not advance, so by night they broke out of the encirclement and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows inside the fortifications ran out and the Liang relief force never came. In the dark of night they broke through the siege lines and escaped.

sentences.zh: 一日一夜，乃出魏境。

translations.literal: In one day and one night, they then left Wei territory.
translations.idiomatic: After a full day and night of flight, they crossed out of Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 至渣口，眾尚萬餘人，馬二千匹。

translations.literal: On reaching Zhakou, the host still numbered more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Zhakou, they still had more than ten thousand men and two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 將入南，士卒竟夜悲歌，侃乃謝曰；

translations.literal: About to enter the south, the soldiers all night sang songs of grief; Kan then took leave saying:
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to cross into the south, the men wept and sang through the night. Kan dismissed them, saying:

sentences.zh: 「卿等懷土，幸適去留。」

translations.literal: "You all are attached to your native soil — I gladly leave the choice of going or staying to you.
translations.idiomatic: "You long for home. Choose freely whether to go on with me or turn back.

sentences.zh: 各拜辭而去。

translations.literal: Each bowed in farewell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They took their leave one by one and went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 侃以大通三年至建鄴，授徐州刺史，並其兄默及三弟忱、給、元皆拜刺史。

translations.literal: Kan in the third year of Datong arrived at Jianye; he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou, and together with his elder brother Mo and his three younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan all were invested as governors.
translations.idiomatic: Kan reached Jianye in the third year of Datong. He was made governor of Xuzhou, and his elder brother Mo and younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan were each given a provincial governorship as well.

sentences.zh: 侃封高昌縣侯，累遷太子左衛率，中。

translations.literal: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸樂游苑，侃預宴。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Leyou Park; Kan was present at the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Leyou Park, Kan was among those invited to the feast.

sentences.zh: 時少府奏新造兩刃矟成，長二丈四尺，圍一尺三寸。

translations.literal: At that time the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues reported that a newly made double-edged spear was complete — length two zhang four chi, girth one chi three cun.
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain of Palace Revenues announced that a new double-edged spear had been completed: twenty-four feet long with a shaft a foot and three inches around.

sentences.zh: 帝因賜侃河南國紫騮令試之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon bestowed on Kan a purple stallion from Henan Commandery and ordered him to test it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Kan a famed purple horse from Henan and told him to put the weapon through its paces.

sentences.zh: 侃執矟上馬，左右擊刺，特盡其妙。

translations.literal: Kan took the spear, mounted, and thrust and stabbed to left and right, displaying its artistry to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Kan mounted with the spear in hand and struck right and left with perfect mastery of the weapon.

sentences.zh: 觀者登樹。

translations.literal: Those watching climbed trees.
translations.idiomatic: Spectators scrambled up into the trees for a better view.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此樹必為侍中折矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This tree will surely be broken by the Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked, "That tree won't survive the Attendant-in-Ordinary's display.

sentences.zh: 俄而果折，因號此矟為折樹矟。

translations.literal: Before long it indeed broke, and so this spear was named the Tree-Breaking Spear.
translations.idiomatic: Sure enough, the tree soon snapped, and from then on the spear was called the Tree-Breaker.

sentences.zh: 北人降者，唯侃是衣冠餘緒，帝寵之踰於他者，謂曰：「朕少時捉矟，形勢似卿，今失其舊體，殊覺不奇。」

translations.literal: Among northerners who had surrendered, only Kan was descended from the robe-and-cap elite; the emperor favored him beyond the others and said: "In my youth when I wielded the spear my form resembled yours; now having lost my former build, I find it quite lacking in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the northern defectors, only Kan came from the old gentry in cap and gown. The emperor favored him above the rest and said, "When I was young my spear-play looked much like yours. These days I've lost that old form, and by comparison nothing seems quite so marvelous.

sentences.zh: 上又制武宴詩三十韻示侃，侃即席上應詔。

translations.literal: The emperor also composed a thirty-rhyme Martial Banquet Poem and showed it to Kan; Kan immediately at the feast responded to the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then composed a thirty-couplet poem for the martial banquet and presented it to Kan, who answered on the spot from his seat.

sentences.zh: 帝覽曰：「吾聞仁者有勇，今見勇者有仁，可謂鄒、魯遺風，英賢不絕。」

translations.literal: The emperor on reading said: "I have heard that the benevolent have courage; now I see one courageous who also has benevolence — truly the lingering wind of Zou and Lu, noble worthies never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After reading it the emperor said, "They say the humane are brave; today I see bravery joined with humanity — the spirit of the sages of Zou and Lu still lives, and worthy men are not extinct.

sentences.zh: 是日詔入直殿省，啟尚方仗不堪用。

translations.literal: That day he was ordered to enter and stand duty in the Palace Secretariat; he reported that the arsenal weapons were unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was ordered into attendance at the Palace Secretariat, where he reported that the weapons in the imperial armory were shoddy and unusable.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，坐者非一。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; more than one person present was punished.
