translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, and several officials present were held accountable.

sentences.zh: 及侯景作逆，果弊於仗粗。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, they indeed suffered disaster from the crude quality of the weapons.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, the dynasty paid dearly for those worthless arms.

sentences.zh: 後遷都官尚書，尚書令何敬容用事，與之並省，未嘗遊造。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Justice; Minister-in-Chief He Jingrong held power; sharing the same ministry with him, Kan never paid social visits.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Justice. He Jingrong, the chief minister, dominated the court, but though they served in the same ministry, Kan never once called on him socially.

sentences.zh: 左衛蘭欽同侍宮宴，詞色少交，侃於坐折之曰：「小子！

translations.literal: Left Guard Lan Qin attended the palace banquet together with him; in words and expression they had little exchange; Kan at the seat rebuked him, saying: "Boy!
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Lan Qin shared a palace banquet with him but barely exchanged a courteous word. Kan publicly dressed him down: "You brat!

sentences.zh: 汝以銅鼓買朱異作父，韋粲作兄，何敢無宜適。」

translations.literal: You used copper drums to buy Zhu Yi as a father and Wei Can as an elder brother — how dare you be so utterly without propriety!
translations.idiomatic: You traded copper drums to buy yourself Zhu Yi for a patron and Wei Can for a brother — how dare you behave with such shameless impudence!

sentences.zh: 朱時在席。

translations.literal: Zhu was at the time present at the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi was sitting right there at the table.

sentences.zh: 後華林法會，欽拜謝於省中。

translations.literal: Later at a Huashlin Buddhist assembly, Qin bowed in apology within the ministry offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a Buddhist rite at Huashlin Park, Qin came to the ministry to offer his apologies.

sentences.zh: 王銓謂欽曰：「卿能屈膝廉公，彌見盡美；

translations.literal: Wang Quan said to Qin: "Your ability to bend the knee before Lord Lian shows your virtues to fullest perfection;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan told Qin, "Your willingness to humble yourself before the old general shows real grace;

sentences.zh: 然羊公意猶未釋，容能更置一拜？」

translations.literal: yet Lord Yang's mind is still not eased — might you perhaps offer one more bow?
translations.idiomatic: but Lord Yang's displeasure may not yet be spent. Could you manage one more bow?

sentences.zh: 欽從之。

translations.literal: Qin complied.
translations.idiomatic: Qin did as he was advised.

sentences.zh: 宦者張僧胤嘗候侃，侃曰：「我床非閹人所坐。」

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Sengyin once came to visit Kan; Kan said: "My couch is not a seat for castrated men.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Zhang Sengyin once came calling, Kan said, "My bed is no place for a eunuch to sit.

sentences.zh: 竟不前之。

translations.literal: In the end he did not advance to it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang never took another step toward it.

sentences.zh: 時論美其貞正。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time praised his integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion admired his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，為侍中，會大舉北侵，以侃為冠軍將軍，監作寒山堰事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he became Attendant-in-Ordinary; coinciding with a great northern campaign, Kan was made General Who Establishes Might and supervised construction of the Hanshan Dam.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary. When the court launched a major invasion of the north, Kan was appointed General Who Establishes Might and put in charge of building the Hanshan Dam.

sentences.zh: 堰立，侃勸元帥貞陽侯明乘水攻彭城，不見納。

translations.literal: When the dam was completed, Kan urged the commander, the Marquis of Zhenyang, Ming, to exploit the water and attack Pengcheng, but the advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dam was finished, Kan urged the commander, Marquis Zhenyang Ming, to strike Pengcheng while the floodwaters held, but his counsel was rejected.

sentences.zh: 既而魏援大至，侃頻言乘其遠來可擊，旦日又勸出戰，並不從。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Wei reinforcements arrived in force; Kan repeatedly said that while they had come from afar they could be struck; the next morning he again urged battle — none of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei reinforcements arrived in strength, Kan kept insisting that troops so far from home could be beaten on arrival. The next day he urged battle again, but every recommendation was ignored.

sentences.zh: 侃乃率所領頓堰上。

translations.literal: Kan then led the troops under his command and encamped on the dam.
translations.idiomatic: Kan withdrew with his own command and held the dam.

sentences.zh: 及眾軍敗，侃結陣徐還。

translations.literal: When the allied armies were defeated, Kan formed ranks and withdrew at a measured pace.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force collapsed, Kan kept his men in formation and fell back in good order.

sentences.zh: 二年，復為都官尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he again became Minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 侯景反，攻陷曆陽，帝問侃討景之策。

translations.literal: Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and the emperor asked Kan for a strategy to suppress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang, the emperor asked Kan how best to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 侃求以二千人急據採石，令邵陵王襲取壽春，使景進不得前，退失巢窟，烏合之眾，自然瓦解。

translations.literal: Kan requested two thousand men to seize Caishi in haste, and ordered the Prince of Shaoling to strike and take Shouchun, so that Jing advancing could not proceed and retreating would lose his nest — the mob gathered at random would naturally disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: Kan asked for two thousand men to seize Caishi immediately and urged the Prince of Shaoling to take Shouchun by surprise, so Hou Jing could neither advance nor retreat to a secure base; his ragtag following would fall apart on its own.

sentences.zh: 議者謂景未敢便逼都，遂寢其策。

translations.literal: Those in council said Jing would not dare promptly press on the capital, and so his plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The counsellors argued that Hou Jing would never dare march straight on the capital, and Kan's plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 令王質往。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was ordered to go instead.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Wang Zhi in his place.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「今茲敗矣。」

translations.literal: Kan said: "This time we are defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "We've lost already.

sentences.zh: 乃令侃率千餘騎頓望國門。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to lead more than a thousand horsemen and encamp facing the Capital Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was then ordered to take a thousand-plus cavalry and hold position before the Capital Gate.

sentences.zh: 景至新林，追侃入副宣城王都督城內諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was urgently summoned to enter the city as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in directing all military affairs within the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was rushed inside to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in commanding the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 時景既卒至，百姓競入，公私混亂，無復次序。

translations.literal: At that time Jing had arrived so suddenly that common people rushed in together; public and private affairs were in chaos, with order no longer preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing had struck with no warning. People thronged into the city in panic, public and private affairs collapsed into chaos, and every trace of order vanished.

sentences.zh: 侃乃區分防擬，皆以宗室間之。

translations.literal: Kan then divided defensive positions, interposing members of the imperial clan throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Kan organized the defenses sector by sector, placing members of the imperial clan at intervals throughout the lines.

sentences.zh: 軍人爭入武庫，自取器甲，所司不能禁，侃命斬數人方得止。

translations.literal: Soldiers vied to enter the armory and take weapons and armor for themselves; the responsible officials could not stop them — Kan ordered several men executed before it could be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers stormed the armory and helped themselves to arms; the officers on duty could not restrain them until Kan had several men executed.

sentences.zh: 是時梁興四十七年，境內無事，公卿在位，及閭里士大夫莫見兵甲。

translations.literal: At this time the Liang dynasty had risen for forty-seven years; within the borders all was peaceful; high ministers in office and town and village gentlemen had never seen arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang had enjoyed forty-seven years of peace. Within the realm nothing threatened; ministers at court and gentlemen in every lane had never once seen weapons of war.

sentences.zh: 賊至卒迫，公私駭震。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived so suddenly and pressed closely, public and private parties were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy suddenly appeared at the gates, court and city alike were struck with terror.

sentences.zh: 時宿將已盡，後進少年並出在外，城中唯有侃及柳津、韋黯。

translations.literal: At that time the veteran generals were already exhausted; younger successors were all abroad; within the city there remained only Kan together with Liu Jin and Wei An.
translations.idiomatic: The old commanders were gone, the rising generation was away on campaign, and within the walls only Kan, Liu Jin, and Wei An remained.

sentences.zh: 津年老且疾，黯懦而無謀，軍旅指撝，一決於侃，膽力俱壯，簡文深仗之。

translations.literal: Jin was aged and ill; An was timid and without strategy; command of the army rested entirely with Kan; his courage and strength were both vigorous; Emperor Jianwen deeply relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was old and sick, Wei An timid and without counsel. Every military decision fell to Kan alone. Bold and resolute, he was the man on whom Emperor Jianwen staked the city's survival.

sentences.zh: 及賊逼城，眾皆兇懼，侃偽稱得外射書，云：「邵陵、西昌侯已至近路」，眾乃少安。

translations.literal: When the rebels pressed the city, all were fiercely afraid; Kan falsely claimed to have received a letter shot in from outside, saying: "The Prince of Shaoling and the Marquis of Xichang have already reached the near road" — the masses then were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy closed on the walls, panic spread through the ranks. Kan feigned receipt of a message brought in by arrow, claiming that the Prince of Shaoling and the Marquis of Xichang were already on the road nearby. The troops steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 賊攻東掖門，縱火甚盛。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked the East Side Gate and set fires that burned very fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels assaulted the East Side Gate and raised a tremendous blaze.

sentences.zh: 侃以水沃滅火，射殺數人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Kan extinguished the fire by dousing it with water, shot and killed several men, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Kan drowned the flames with water, brought down several of the enemy with his bow, and the attack broke off.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、軍師將軍。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally named Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Army.

sentences.zh: 有詔送金五千兩、銀萬兩、絹萬匹賜戰士。

translations.literal: An edict ordered gold five thousand taels, silver ten thousand taels, and silk ten thousand bolts sent to reward the fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree sent five thousand taels of gold, ten thousand taels of silver, and ten thousand bolts of silk to reward the defenders.

sentences.zh: 侃辭不受，部曲千餘人並私加賞賚。

translations.literal: Kan declined and did not accept; he personally added rewards for more than a thousand men of his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: Kan refused the imperial grant and instead paid rewards out of his own purse to the thousand-odd men of his retinue.

sentences.zh: 賊為尖頂木驢攻城，矢石所不能制。

translations.literal: The rebels built pointed-top wooden siege towers to attack the city; arrows and stones could not check them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rolled up pointed wooden siege towers against the walls — neither arrows nor stones could stop them.

sentences.zh: 侃作雉尾炬，施鐵鏃，以油灌之，擲驢上焚之俄盡。

translations.literal: Kan made pheasant-tail torches, fitted them with iron arrowheads, soaked them in oil, and cast them onto the towers to burn them — in no time they were consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Kan devised fire arrows shaped like pheasant tails, tipped with iron and soaked in oil, and hurled them onto the towers until the structures blazed up and were gone.

sentences.zh: 賊又東西起二土山以臨城，城中震駭。

translations.literal: The rebels again raised two earthen mounds east and west to overlook the city; within the city there was shock and terror.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then piled up two earthen hills east and west to dominate the walls, throwing the city into alarm.

sentences.zh: 侃命為地道，潛引其土山，不能立。

translations.literal: Kan ordered tunnels dug to secretly undermine their earthen mounds so they could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: Kan had his men dig tunnels beneath the hills to undermine them, and the mounds collapsed before they could be finished.

sentences.zh: 賊又作登城樓車，高十餘丈，欲臨射城中。

translations.literal: The rebels also built wall-scaling tower wagons more than ten zhang high, intending to overlook and shoot into the city.
translations.idiomatic: They next built siege towers more than a hundred feet high, intending to fire down into the city.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「車高塹虛，彼來必倒，可臥而觀之。」

translations.literal: Kan said: "The wagon is tall and the moat is hollow — when they come it is sure to topple; one may lie down and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Those towers are too tall for hollow ground at the moat's edge. When they roll forward they'll tip over. We can lie back and watch.

sentences.zh: 及車動果倒，眾皆服焉。

translations.literal: When the wagon moved it indeed toppled; all were convinced.
translations.idiomatic: When the towers advanced they fell exactly as he had predicted, and everyone acknowledged his judgment.

sentences.zh: 賊既頻攻不捷，乃築長圍。

translations.literal: Since the rebels had repeatedly attacked without success, they then built a long encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated assaults failed, the rebels settled in to build a full circumvallation.

sentences.zh: 朱異、張綰議出擊之。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie against the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 帝以問侃，侃曰：「不可，賊多日攻城，既不能下，故立長圍，欲引城中降者耳。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Kan; Kan said: "It cannot be done. The rebels have besieged for many days and could not take the city, so they establish a long encirclement intending only to lure those in the city who would surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Kan's view. Kan said, "No. They have failed to take the city by assault, so they are building a long siege line to tempt defectors inside the walls — that is all.

sentences.zh: 今擊之，出人若少，不足破賊；

translations.literal: If we strike now and send out few men, it is insufficient to break the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: If we sortie with too few men, we won't break them;

sentences.zh: 若多，則一旦失利，門隘橋小，必大致挫衄。」

translations.literal: if many, then once defeated the gates are narrow and the bridges small — there will surely be great rout and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: but if we send out many and lose, the gates are narrow and the bridges small — a retreat would become a slaughter.

sentences.zh: 不從，遂使千餘人出戰。

translations.literal: The advice was not followed; more than a thousand men were then sent out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was ignored, and more than a thousand men were sent out to fight.

sentences.zh: 未及交鋒，望風退走，果以爭橋赴水，死者太半。

translations.literal: Before they could cross blades they fled at sight of the enemy; indeed in the scramble for the bridge they plunged into the water — more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: They never even closed with the enemy but broke and ran. In the crush at the bridge men tumbled into the water, and more than half perished.

sentences.zh: 初，侃長子鷟為景所獲，執來城下示侃。

translations.literal: At the outset Kan's eldest son Zhuo was captured by Jing; he was brought beneath the walls to show Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the siege Hou Jing captured Kan's eldest son Zhuo and brought him beneath the walls for his father to see.

sentences.zh: 侃謂曰：「我傾宗報主，猶恨不足，豈復計此一子。

translations.literal: Kan said to him: "I pour out my clan to repay my lord — still I regret it is not enough; how could I again reckon this one son?
translations.idiomatic: Kan called out, "I have offered my whole house to serve my sovereign and still regret it is too little. Why should I weigh the life of one son?

sentences.zh: 幸早殺之。」

translations.literal: I hope you will kill him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Be done with him at once.

sentences.zh: 數日復持來，侃謂鷟曰：「久以汝為死，猶在邪？

translations.literal: Several days later he was brought again; Kan said to Zhuo: "Long I thought you dead — yet you still live?
translations.idiomatic: Days later they brought the boy before the wall again. Kan said to Zhuo, "I had long taken you for dead — you still breathe?

sentences.zh: 吾以身許國，誓死行陣，終不以爾而生進退。」

translations.literal: I have pledged my body to the state, sworn to die in the battle line; in the end I will not for your sake advance or retreat in life."
translations.idiomatic: I have given my life to the realm and sworn to die where I stand. I will never let your fate dictate whether I hold or yield."

sentences.zh: 因引弓射之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew his bow and shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: He nocked an arrow and fired at his own son.

sentences.zh: 賊以其忠義，亦弗之害。

translations.literal: The rebels because of his loyalty and righteousness also did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his fidelity, the enemy did not harm the boy.

sentences.zh: 景遣儀同傅士哲呼侃與語，曰：「侯王遠來問訊天子，何為閉拒不時進納？

translations.literal: Jing sent Palace Attendant Fellow Fu Shizhe to summon Kan and speak with him, saying: "The Marquis-King has come from afar to inquire after the Son of Heaven — why do you shut the gates and refuse timely admission?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent the palace attendant fellow Fu Shizhe to call Kan out for a parley. "The prince-regent has journeyed far to pay his respects to the Son of Heaven," he said. "Why do you keep your gates barred and withhold timely access?

sentences.zh: 尚書國家大臣，宜啟朝廷。」

translations.literal: As Minister of the Masters of Writing, a great minister of the state, you ought to open the gates for the court.
translations.idiomatic: You are a minister of the realm — you should open the gates for the court's sake.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「侯將軍奔亡之後，歸命國家，重鎮方城，懸相任寄，何所患苦，忽致稱兵，豈有人臣而至於此。

translations.literal: Kan said: "After the Marquis-General fled and wandered, he submitted to the state, held the heavy post at Fangcheng, and was entrusted with great responsibility from afar — what grievance could he suffer that he would suddenly raise arms? Could any minister reach such a point?
translations.idiomatic: Kan replied, "After your flight you submitted to the dynasty, were given the weighty post at Fangcheng, and entrusted with command from afar. What complaint could justify suddenly taking up arms? Has any loyal minister ever stooped to this?

sentences.zh: 吾不能妄受浮說，開門揖盜。」

translations.literal: I cannot rashly accept empty talk and open the gates to invite robbers in."
translations.idiomatic: I will not swallow idle promises and open the gates to welcome a thief."

sentences.zh: 士哲曰：「在北之日，久挹風猷，願去戎服，得一相見。」

translations.literal: Shizhe said: "In the days in the north, long I admired your manner and virtue; I wish to remove my military garb and meet you face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe said, "When I was in the north I long admired your reputation. I would lay aside my armor — let me see you once."

sentences.zh: 侃為免胄，士哲瞻望久之而去，其為北人所欽慕如此。

translations.literal: Kan removed his helmet for him; Shizhe gazed long and then departed — such was the admiration he won among northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Kan doffed his helmet. Shizhe stared a long while before he left — that was how deeply the northerners revered him.

sentences.zh: 後大雨，城內土山崩，賊乘之垂入，苦戰不能禁。

translations.literal: Later came heavy rain; the earthen hills within the city collapsed, the rebels seized the moment and nearly entered — bitter fighting could not check them.
translations.idiomatic: Later heavy rains caused the earthen siege mounds inside the walls to collapse. The rebels pressed the breach and nearly broke through; despite fierce fighting the defenders could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 侃乃令多擲火，為火城以斷其路，徐於城內築城，賊不能進。

translations.literal: Kan then ordered much fire cast down, making a fire-wall to cut off their path, and slowly built an inner wall within the city — the rebels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kan ordered a barrage of fire, forming a wall of flame to block the way, then slowly raised a second wall inside the city. The enemy could advance no farther.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾卒於城內，贈侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness within the city; posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness inside the walls. He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 子球嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qiu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiu inherited his position.

sentences.zh: 侃少雄勇，膂力絕人，所用弓至二十石，馬上用六石弓。

translations.literal: In youth Kan was heroically brave; his physical strength surpassed other men — the bow he used reached twenty piculs, and mounted he used a six-picul bow.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Kan was fiercely brave, with strength beyond ordinary men. He drew a bow rated at twenty piculs, and on horseback wielded one of six.

sentences.zh: 嘗於兗州堯廟蹋壁，直上至五尋，橫行得七跡。

translations.literal: Once at the Yao Temple in Yan Province he kicked off a wall, ascended straight up to five xun, and walking horizontally left seven footprints.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Temple of Yao in Yan Province he ran up a wall, climbing straight to a height of five xun and leaving seven horizontal footprints as he went.

sentences.zh: 泗橋有數石人，長八尺，大十圍。

translations.literal: At the Si Bridge were several stone figures, eight chi tall and ten wei in girth.
translations.idiomatic: At Si Bridge stood several stone statues eight feet tall and ten arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 侃執以相擊，悉皆破碎。

translations.literal: Kan seized them and struck them against one another — all were utterly shattered.
translations.idiomatic: He picked them up and smashed them together until every one lay in pieces.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，善音律，自造採蓮、棹歌兩曲，甚有新致。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant; skilled in music, he himself composed two pieces, "Plucking Lotus" and "Oar Song," with very fresh elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He was lavish by nature and skilled in music, composing two tunes of his own — "Plucking Lotus" and "Oar Song" — notable for their fresh charm.

sentences.zh: 姬妾列侍，窮極奢靡。

translations.literal: Concubines stood in attendance in rows, luxury pushed to its extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Rows of concubines attended him in consummate extravagance.

sentences.zh: 有彈箏人陸太喜著鹿角爪，長七寸。

translations.literal: There was a zheng-player Lu Taixi who wore deer-antler plectra seven inches long.
translations.idiomatic: One zheng player, Lu Taixi, wore deer-antler finger-picks seven inches long.

sentences.zh: 舞人張淨琬腰圍一尺六寸，時人咸推能掌上舞。

translations.literal: The dancer Zhang Jingwan had a waist one chi six inches around; contemporaries all praised her ability to dance on the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: The dancer Zhang Jingwan measured one chi six inches at the waist; all agreed she could dance upon the palm of one's hand.

sentences.zh: 又有孫荊玉能反腰帖地，銜得席上玉簪。

translations.literal: There was also Sun Jingyu, who could bend her back backward to the ground and take a jade hairpin from the mat in her mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Another, Sun Jingyu, could arch backward until her back touched the floor and pick up a jade hairpin from the mat with her teeth.

sentences.zh: 敕賚歌人王娥兒，東宮亦賚歌者屈偶之，並妙盡奇曲，一時無對。

translations.literal: By imperial order he was granted the singer Wang E'er; the Eastern Palace also granted the singer Qu Ouzhi — both perfectly mastered extraordinary songs, unmatched for a time.
translations.idiomatic: The throne bestowed upon him the singer Wang E'er, and the Eastern Palace granted the singer Qu Ouzhi; both mastered rare songs beyond compare in their day.

sentences.zh: 初赴衡州，於兩艖滏起三間通梁水齋，飾以珠玉，加之錦繢，盛設帷屏，列女樂。

translations.literal: When he first went to Heng Province, on two barges chained together he raised a three-bay waterside pavilion with connecting beams, adorned with pearls and jade, further hung with brocade, lavishly furnished with curtains and screens, and arrayed with female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: When he first set out for Heng Province he had built on two lashed barges a three-bay waterside hall with linked beams, inlaid with pearls and jade, hung with brocades, draped with curtains and screens, and lined with female musicians.

sentences.zh: 乘潮解纜，臨波置酒，緣塘傍水，觀者填咽。

translations.literal: Riding the tide he cast off the moorings, set wine by the waves, and along the embankment beside the water spectators packed the ways choking them.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off with the tide, set out wine upon the water, and as he moved along the embankment the shore was choked with onlookers.

sentences.zh: 大同中，魏使陽斐與侃在北嘗同學，有詔命侃延斐同宴。

translations.literal: In the Datong era the Wei envoy Yang Fei and Kan had once been fellow students in the north; an edict ordered Kan to invite Fei to a banquet together.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong reign Yang Fei, envoy from Wei, had been Kan's schoolmate in the north. An edict directed Kan to entertain him at a feast.

sentences.zh: 賓客三百餘人，食器皆金玉雜寶，奏三部女樂。

translations.literal: Guests numbered more than three hundred; eating vessels were all gold, jade, and mixed treasures; three ensembles of female musicians performed.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred guests attended; every serving piece was gold, jade, or some other treasure, and three companies of female musicians performed.

sentences.zh: 至夕，侍婢百餘人俱執金花燭。

translations.literal: By evening more than a hundred serving maids all held golden-flower candles.
translations.idiomatic: At nightfall more than a hundred maidservants each bore gilt-flower candles.

sentences.zh: 侃不飲酒而好賓遊，終日獻酬，同其醉醒。

translations.literal: Kan did not drink wine but loved entertaining guests; all day he offered toasts, sharing their drunkenness and sobriety.
translations.idiomatic: Kan himself did not drink but loved hosting company; he spent the day raising his cup with them, sharing alike in their revelry and restraint.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，有器局。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and tolerant, with breadth of capacity and vision.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and magnanimous, with the bearing of a man of large design.

sentences.zh: 嘗南還至漣口置酒，有客張孺才者，醉於船中失火，延燒七十餘艘，所燔金帛不可勝數。

translations.literal: Once returning south he reached Lian Mouth and set out wine; a guest named Zhang Rucai, drunk aboard ship, accidentally set fire, which spread to burn more than seventy vessels — the gold and silks consumed were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning south, he halted at Lian Mouth for a banquet. A guest named Zhang Rucai, drunk aboard ship, set a fire that spread to more than seventy vessels; the gold and silks lost were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 侃聞聊不掛意，命酒不輟。

translations.literal: When Kan heard of it he barely gave it a thought and did not cease ordering wine.
translations.idiomatic: Kan barely took notice and never stopped the wine.

sentences.zh: 孺才慚懼自逃，侃慰喻使還，待之如舊。

translations.literal: Rucai, ashamed and afraid, fled on his own; Kan comforted and reasoned with him until he returned, treating him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai fled in shame and fear; Kan calmed him and coaxed him back, treating him exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 第三子從字子鵬，隨侃台內，城陷，竄于陽平。

translations.literal: His third son Cong, styled Zipeng, followed Kan within the Terrace City; when the city fell he fled to Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Cong, courtesy name Zipeng, had been with Kan inside the capital citadel. When the walls fell he fled to Yangping.

sentences.zh: 侯景以其妹為小妻，呼還待之甚厚，以為庫真都督。

translations.literal: Hou Jing took his younger sister as a minor wife, summoned him back and treated him very generously, making him Director of the Palace Armory.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing took Kan's younger sister as a concubine, recalled Cong, treated him handsomely, and appointed him Director of the Palace Armory.

sentences.zh: 及景敗，從密圖之，乃隨其東走。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated, Cong secretly plotted against him and followed him east in flight.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's cause collapsed, Cong plotted against him in secret and went east with him in flight.

sentences.zh: 景於松江戰敗，惟餘三舸，下海欲向蒙山。

translations.literal: Jing was defeated at Song River; only three boats remained; he put to sea intending to head for Meng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was routed on the Song River and left with only three boats. He put out to sea, meaning to make for Meng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 會景晝寢，從語海師：「此中何處有蒙山，汝但聽我處分。」

translations.literal: It happened that Jing napped by day; Cong told the sea pilot: "Where is Meng Mountain here? You need only obey my orders.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Hou Jing was napping by day, Cong told the helmsman, "Where is Meng Mountain in these waters? You need only do as I say.

sentences.zh: 遂直向京口，至胡豆洲，景覺，大驚。

translations.literal: Thereupon they headed straight for Jingkou; reaching Hudu Isle, Jing awoke — greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: He then steered straight for Jingkou. When they reached Hudu Isle Hou Jing woke and was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 問岸上，云：「郭元建猶在廣陵」。

translations.literal: He asked those on shore, who said: "Guo Yuanjian is still at Guangling."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the shore and was told, "Guo Yuanjian is still at Guangling."

sentences.zh: 景大喜，將依之。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly pleased and was about to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was overjoyed and prepared to join him.

sentences.zh: 從拔刀叱海師使向京口。

translations.literal: Cong drew his saber and shouted at the sea pilot to steer toward Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Cong bared his blade and shouted at the helmsman to make for Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 從與王元禮、謝答仁弟葳蕤，並景之昵也，三人謂景曰：「我等為王百戰百勝，自謂無敵，卒至於此，豈非天乎。

translations.literal: Cong, Wang Yuanli, and Xie Daren's younger brother Weirui — all Jing's intimates — the three said to Jing: "We fought a hundred battles for you, a hundred victories, deeming ourselves invincible — yet in the end we come to this. Is it not Heaven's will?
translations.idiomatic: Cong, Wang Yuanli, and Weirui — younger brother of Xie Daren and all three of Hou Jing's favorites — said to him, "We fought a hundred battles for you and won a hundred times. We thought ourselves invincible. To end here — is this not Heaven's decree?

sentences.zh: 今就王乞頭以取富貴。」

translations.literal: Now we beg my lord's head to win wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Grant us your head now, lord, and we shall win fortune and rank.

sentences.zh: 景欲透水，從抽刀斫之。

translations.literal: Jing wished to plunge into the water; Cong drew his blade and hacked at him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing tried to leap into the water; Cong struck at him with his blade.

sentences.zh: 景乃走入船中，以小刀抉船。

translations.literal: Jing then ran into the boat and used a small knife to cut open the hull.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing ran back into the boat and gouged at the hull with a knife.

sentences.zh: 從以矟入刺殺之。

translations.literal: Cong thrust in with a spear and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cong drove a spear through him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 景僕射索超世在別船，葳蕤以景命召之，斬於京口。

translations.literal: Jing's Vice Director Suo Chaoshi was on a separate boat; Weirui summoned him in Jing's name and beheaded him at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's vice director Suo Chaoshi was on another boat. Weirui called him in Hou Jing's name and executed him at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 元帝以從為青州刺史，封昌國縣侯，又領東陽太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan made Cong Inspector of Qing Province, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changguo District, and furthermore had him serve concurrently as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made Cong Inspector of Qing Province, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changguo, and also appointed him Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 征陸納，加散騎常侍，除西晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Lu Na he was additionally made Ordinary Grandee of the Fast Horse, and appointed Inspector of Western Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Lu Na he was promoted to Ordinary Grandee of the Fast Horse and made Inspector of Western Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 破郭元建于東關，遷東晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He defeated Guo Yuanjian at East Pass and was transferred to Inspector of Eastern Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Guo Yuanjian at Dong Pass and was transferred to Inspector of Eastern Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年，西魏圍江陵，從赴援不及。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengsheng, Western Wei besieged Jiangling; Cong hurried to relieve it but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chengsheng Western Wei besieged Jiangling; Cong marched to the rescue but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 從王僧愔征蕭勃於嶺表，聞僧辯敗，乃還，為侯瑱所破，遇害，年二十八。

translations.literal: Following Wang Sengyin's campaign against Xiao Bo in the lands beyond the ridges, on hearing of Senbian's defeat he turned back, was broken by Hou Tian, and met disaster — aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Sengyin against Xiao Bo in Lingnan. Hearing of Senbian's defeat he turned back, was routed by Hou Tian, and was killed — aged twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 羊鴉仁字孝穆，泰山钜平人也。

translations.literal: Yang Ren, styled Xiaomu, was a man of Juping in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren, courtesy name Xiaomu, was a native of Juping in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，仕郡為主簿。

translations.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave; in the commandery he served as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bold and brave and served his commandery as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 並通中，率兄弟自魏歸梁，封廣晉侯。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he led his brothers in coming from Wei to Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era he led his brothers in defecting from Wei to the Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.

sentences.zh: 征伐青、齊間，累有功績，位至都督、北司州刺史。

translations.literal: Campaigning between Qing and Qi he repeatedly achieved merit, rising to Grand Commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns between Qing and Qi he won repeated distinction, rising to area commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 及侯景降，詔鴉仁督土州刺史桓和之、仁州刺史湛海珍等趣縣瓠應接。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Ren to direct Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to hasten to Xuanhuo to link up in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing submitted, Ren was ordered to lead Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to Xuanhuo to coordinate support.

sentences.zh: 景至，仍為都督、司豫二州刺史，鎮縣瓠。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, he remained Grand Commander and Inspector of the two provinces Si and Yu, garrisoning Xuanhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing arrived, Ren remained area commander and Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, holding Xuanhuo.

sentences.zh: 會侯景敗于渦陽，魏軍漸逼，鴉仁恐糧運不繼，遂還北司，上表陳謝。

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang; Wei armies gradually pressed in; Ren feared grain supply would not continue, so he returned to Northern Sizhou and submitted a memorial confessing fault.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang and Wei forces closed in, Ren, fearing his supply lines would fail, withdrew to Northern Sizhou and submitted a confession to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒鴉仁，鴉仁懼，頓軍於淮上。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angry at Ren; Ren was afraid and halted his army on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious with Ren. Afraid, he halted his army on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 及侯景反，鴉仁率所部入援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Ren led his division to enter as relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Ren led his troops to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，景既背盟，鴉仁乃與趙伯超及南康王會理共攻賊於東府城，反為賊敗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Jing having broken the covenant, Ren then with Zhao Bochao and Prince Huili of Nankang jointly attacked the rebels at the Eastern Palace City, but in turn was defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, after Hou Jing broke faith, Ren joined Zhao Bochao and Prince Huili of Nankang in an assault on the rebels at the Eastern Palace City — and was driven back.

sentences.zh: 台城陷，景以為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Jing made him Minister of the Five Arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital citadel fell, Hou Jing appointed him Minister of the Five Arms.

sentences.zh: 鴉仁常思奮發，謂所親曰：「吾以凡流，受寵朝廷，竟無報效，以答重恩。

translations.literal: Ren constantly thought of rousing himself to action; he said to those close to him: "I am but ordinary stock, yet favored by the court — in the end I have no merit to repay, to answer this heavy grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ren long burned to redeem himself. He told his intimates, "I am no one extraordinary, yet the court has heaped favor on me. I have never repaid that debt.

sentences.zh: 今若以此終，沒有餘責。」

translations.literal: If I were to end thus now, I would have no further account to answer for.
translations.idiomatic: If I die like this, I will have nothing left to answer for.

sentences.zh: 因泣下，見者傷焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon tears fell; those who saw it were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke, and all who heard him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 三年，出奔江西，將赴江陵，至東莞，為故北徐州刺史荀伯道子晷所害。

translations.literal: In the third year he fled to Jiangxi, intending to go to Jiangling; reaching Dongguan, he was killed by Xi Gui, son of the former Inspector of Northern Xuzhou Xun Bodao.
translations.idiomatic: the third year of In he fled west into Jiangxi, bound for Jiangling. At Dongguan he was murdered by Xi Gui, son of the former Inspector of Northern Xuzhou Xun Bodao.

sentences.zh: 臨死以報效不終，因而泣下。

translations.literal: At the point of death, because his repayment of service would not reach completion, he wept.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, he wept that he could not finish repaying his debt of service.

sentences.zh: 後鴉仁兄子海珍知之，掘晷父伯道並祖及所生母合五喪，各分其半骨，共棺焚之，半骨雜他骨，作五袋盛之，銘袋上曰：「荀晷祖父母某之骨」

translations.literal: Later Ren's elder brother's son Haizhen learned of it; he exhumed Gui's father Bodao, grandfather, and natural mother — five coffins in all — split each set of bones in half, placed them in a common coffin and burned them, mixed half the bones with other bones, made five bags to hold them, and inscribed on the bags: "The bones of Xi Gui's paternal grandparents So-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: Later Ren's nephew Haizhen learned what had happened. He exhumed Xi Gui's father Bodao, his grandfather, and the mother who bore him — five graves in all — split each skeleton in half, burned the halves together in one coffin, mixed the remaining halves with other bones, packed them in five bags, and wrote on each bag: "The bones of Xi Gui's grandparents So-and-so."

sentences.zh: 鴉仁子亮，侯景亂後移至吳州刺史，隨王琳，以名將子見禮甚隆。

translations.literal: Ren's son Liang, after Hou Jing's chaos was removed to Inspector of Wu Province, followed Wang Lin, and because he was a famous general's son was received with very lofty courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren's son Liang, after the Hou Jing turmoil, was posted as Inspector of Wu Province; he followed Wang Lin and, as a famous general's son, was treated with the greatest honor.

sentences.zh: 為人多酒無賴，酒醉為閹豎所殺。

translations.literal: As a man he drank much and was reckless; drunk, he was killed by a eunuch attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily and lived dissolutely; one night, drunk, a palace eunuch killed him.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王神念、羊侃、羊鴉仁等，自北徂南，咸受寵任。

translations.literal: The comment says: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren, and others — from the north going south — all received favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren, and others all came south from the north and won the throne's confidence.

sentences.zh: 既而侃及鴉仁晚遇屯剝。

translations.literal: Subsequently Kan and Ren in their later years encountered obstruction and decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kan and Ren met hardship and ruin in their later years.

sentences.zh: 侃則臨危不撓，鴉仁則守義以殞。

translations.literal: Kan then faced peril without bending; Ren then kept righteousness and perished for it.
translations.idiomatic: Kan stood unyielding in the face of death; Ren held to his duty and died for it.

sentences.zh: 古人所謂「心同鐵石」，此之謂乎。

translations.literal: What the ancients called "hearts like iron and stone" — is this not the meaning?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what the ancients meant by "hearts as iron and stone"?

sentences.zh: 僧辯風格秀舉，有文武奇才，而逢茲酷濫，幾致隕覆。

translations.literal: Senbian's manner was refined and elevated; he had extraordinary talent in civil and military affairs — yet he met this cruel flood and nearly came to ruin and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Senbian was graceful and commanding, gifted in both letters and arms, yet he met this cataclysm and nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 幸全首領，卒樹奇功，事人之道，於斯為得。

translations.literal: Fortunately he preserved his head and neck; in the end he raised extraordinary achievement — the way of serving others, in this he attained it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept his life, and in the end won a great victory — in the art of serving one's lord, he had done it right.

sentences.zh: 及時鐘交喪，地居元宰，內有奧主而外求君，遂使尊卑易位，親疏貿序，既同兒戲，且類弈棋。

translations.literal: But when the times ran to mutual loss, he occupied the seat of chief minister — within there was a hidden master and outward he sought a lord — so that high and low exchanged places, near and far reversed their order; it was both like child's play and resembled a game of weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when calamity struck he was chief minister — deferring to a hidden power within while hunting for a patron without — until rank and loyalty traded places, intimacy and distance were scrambled, and governance became child's play, chess on a board.

sentences.zh: 延敵開釁，實基於此，喪國傾宗，為天下笑。

translations.literal: Inviting the enemy and opening strife — the foundation lay truly in this; losing the state and toppling the clan, he became the laughingstock of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Inviting enemies and opening the way to rebellion — that was where it began. The realm was lost, the house fell, and all under heaven laughed.

sentences.zh: 豈天將啟陳，何斯人而斯謬也，哀哉！

translations.literal: Was Heaven about to open the way for Chen? How could such a man be so mistaken — alas!
translations.idiomatic: Was Heaven itself preparing to raise Chen? How could such a man err so gravely? Alas!
